Latest Update: Your Expert-Backed Guide to Preparing for Top Surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1638 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

It has been revealed that getting ready to go under the knife can be scary—even when it’s for a procedure you’ve wanted for as long as you can remember. If you’re preparing for top surgery (a gender-affirming chest surgery to remove or augment breast tissue) right now, chances are you’re probably trying to ease your pre-op anxiety by googling every question you can possibly think of. And that’s normal! But it can also lead you down some deep, dark Reddit threads that’ll do nothing but amplify your nerves.

If you’re wondering how to prepare for top surgery without all the panic-inducing anecdotes, you’ve come to the right place. I chatted with three experts and got their best advice on how to get ready for the procedure while preserving your peace of mind.

Before we get into the tips, keep in mind that the most key part of preparing for top surgery is choosing the right surgeon for you. In addition to finding an experienced and gender-affirming doctor, you’ll want to pick someone who can give you the results you’re looking for. “The techniques your surgeon will use can vary quite a lot depending on your breast size and shape, the texture and quality of your skin, and your goals for the procedure,” explains Eric Plemons, PhD, an associate professor of anthropology and cochair of the Transgender Studies Research Cluster at the University of Arizona.

To make sure you’ll be happy with your results, he suggests watching YouTube videos showcasing before-and-afters and looking at post-surgery images online to help you get an idea of what you want. Then be sure to find a surgeon who understands your goals—if they seem like they’re not listening to you, ditch them. Once you’ve made an appointment with a surgeon you trust, here’s everything else the experts recommend doing to prepare for top surgery.

It has been revealed that this might seem like a no-brainer, but it’s worth mentioning. Before your surgery, your doctor’s office will normally provide you with instructions on what to do before and after the procedure. They typically include info on dietary guidelines, activity restrictions, wound care, and any medications you might need. Make sure that you read all of the information carefully, and keep it handy for the recovery process. “Following these instructions diligently significantly improves surgical outcomes and ensures a smoother recovery,” explains Scott Mosser, MD, FACS, a plastic surgeon who performs gender confirmation surgery and the founder of The Gender Confirmation Center of San Francisco.

According to recent reports, top surgery is a major surgery, and you’ll likely spend the first one to two weeks at home resting after the procedure. So it’s a good idea to prep your space accordingly. Make sure you’ve got a cozy couch or bed setup ready, and consider getting a mastectomy pillow to make lounging and sleeping more comfortable. The Trans Health Program at Fenway Health also recommends getting other items like a long phone charger, a grabber tool, and a back scratcher to make recovery go a bit smoother.

Sources indicate that also, keep in mind that you’re not supposed to lift your arms above your head in the days following top surgery. To make that easier to navigate, consider moving food and essentials to lower, easy-to-reach spots, suggests Plemons.

In a recent development, the last thing you want to do is spend your recovery period stressing about going back to your job. Be sure you request enough time off to allow yourself to truly rest and heal. Exactly how much time you’ll need to spend OOO varies from person to person, so it’s a good idea to chat it through with your surgeon at one of your pre-op appointments.

One of the main factors that determines how long you’ll need to take off work is how physically demanding your job is. You’ll have restricted movement in the weeks after your surgery, and you won’t be able to lift heavy objects, which could impact your responsibilities, depending on your line of work. “I generally ask patients to identify the most physically strenuous aspect of their job, and together we determine an appropriate leave period,” explains Dr. Mosser.

According to recent reports, for your post-op wardrobe, you’ll want a stack of loose-fitting shirts that are easy to put on and take off without raising your arms. (Yup, t-shirts might be off the table for a bit.) Button-up and zip-up options will be your best friends during the recovery period. The loose-fitting aspect is also important because you may need space for surgical drain tubes under your shirt. Tops with interior pockets can also be helpful if you do end up with drains, notes Dr. Mosser. And heads-up: Your shirts might get stained during the healing process, so Plemons recommends grabbing some options from the thrift store so that you’re not worried about ruining them.

In a recent development, in order to help your skin adjust post-surgery, you may want to get an emollient-infused moisturizer like Bio-Oil or Palmer’s Cocoa Butter Lotion. As long as it’s okay with your doctor, you can even start applying these one to two weeks before the procedure to start prepping your skin, if you’d like. After the surgery, Dr. Mosser recommends using one of these moisturizers on your chest every morning and evening—but be careful to avoid your incision sites. This will help with skin relaxation and reduce the appearance of stretch marks, if that’s something you’re concerned about, he explains.

Sources indicate that double-check with your surgeon, but after any scabs from the surgery have fallen off, you should also be able to start using silicone scar tape. Dr. Mosser suggests using it for three months to help optimize healing.

If you vape or smoke cigarettes or weed, you’ll need to quit ahead of your top surgery. The American College of Surgeons recommends quitting smoking four to six weeks before any major surgery and staying smoke-free for at least four weeks post-op to lower your risk of complications, and most doctors require a similar timeline for top surgery.

The stakes are high: According to the Gender Confirmation Center of San Francisco, smoking increases the risk of anesthesia complications and postoperative complications like losing a nipple graft, which can require additional surgery to fix. It also delays healing, which can prolong the recovery process and make it more uncomfortable. Dr. Mosser requires all of his patients to stop smoking for at least three weeks before and after top surgery—no exceptions.

You’ll need some help taking care of yourself and your basic needs in the days following top surgery, so talk to your friends and/or family in advance to put together a initiative. “We’ve consistently seen better outcomes in patients who have a positive, supportive presence in their lives. The best way to ensure this support is to communicate openly with loved ones in advance, set clear expectations about what assistance might be needed, and cultivate an environment of encouragement and care,” Dr. Mosser says.

It has been revealed that decide who’s going to drive you home after the procedure (you won’t be allowed to drive yourself), and think about who might be a good fit to help you with activities like getting dressed and showering the first few days, suggests Plemons. You’ll probably also need someone to help you with tasks like meal prep, medication reminders, carrying groceries, and caring for any pets for a bit.

In a recent development, in addition to logistical support, you’ll likely need some emotional support during the top surgery process. The procedure is often something you’ve been anticipating for a long time, and it can be an emotional experience. “Such a big event comes with big feelings about your body, about yourself, and about your future,” claims Plemons. So think about who you plan to lean on for support as you navigate your feelings both pre- and post-op. Staying connected to your community—whether that be friends, chosen family, or an online community—is really crucial. “Even small moments of support, like check-ins or affirming conversations, can make a huge difference in feeling cared for during recovery,” adds Jesse Kahn, LCSW-R, CST, director and sex therapist at the Gender & Sexuality Therapy Center in Upcoming York.

“Top surgery is a significant emotional and physical milestone, and a range of feelings—excitement, anxiety, or unexpected emotions—are completely normal,” explains Kahn. They recommend giving yourself permission to feel and process your emotions without judgment or criticism. Your emotional support network can help with this, but if you’re already seeing a therapist you may want to schedule a session early on in your recovery. “[A therapy session] can be a good opportunity to just check in, look inward, reflect on what you’re experiencing, and give space for your emotions,” notes Kahn. Practicing self-care, managing expectations, and doing activities that bring you comfort are also very vital during the top surgery process, they add.

Give yourself something you look forward to by thinking about what you want to wear once you’ve healed. Buy a shirt in a style you’ve always wanted to wear, or strategy out an outfit that’ll showcase your post-op body. “Choose something that will fit you well and show off the body you’re excited to have," suggests Plemons. "After soreness and swelling, it is amazing how gratifying it is to slip into that special shirt (or strut around in no shirt at all).”.

In a recent development, this article is not intended to be a substitute for medical advice. Always seek the advice of your doctor or other qualified health professional with any questions you may have regarding surgery.

  • According to recent reports, while the sci-fi series takes place some 73 years in the future, Schafer turned back a couple decades for the first day of her press junket.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

2026 has had no shortage of press tours. From The Devil Wears Prada 2 to The Odyssey to Euphoria to The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, it’s been a year of global rollouts and method dressing. And we’re not quite done yet.

In a recent development, earlier this week, Hunter Schafer kicked off the Blade Runner 2099 promo at the Los Angeles premiere in a custom Prada leather micro dress and voluminous fur coat—and since then, she’s been bringing her A game to the miniseries’ press. Working with stylist Dara, the Euphoria actor has revealed up in straight-off-the-runway pulls and vintage finds alike, piecing together a dynamic collection of ensembles as she counts down the days to the November 25 release date.

According to recent reports, while the sci-fi series takes place some 73 years in the future, Schafer turned back a couple decades for the first day of her press junket. Working with Dara once again, the actor was seen wearing a full look from the Undercover Fall/Winter 2007 collection.

Sources indicate that the Y2K ensemble was composed of a handful of neutral layers, including a turtleneck base, a long-sleeve ribbed knit top with sheer accents, and little micro shorts in chocolate brown. She wore ear muffs and her hair in pigtails, and tucked her semi-sheer thigh-high stockings into black-and-brown wedges.

Later, the star switched gears, selecting a vibrant color-blocked minidress from Zane Li’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection for Lii. The high-contrast runway piece saw a bright-teal shift dress with a square neckline and spaghetti straps, layered with an open-back coral-orange piece with a similar silhouette. (See photos here.).

Industry observers note that out at the end of the month, Blade Runner 2099 takes place half a century after the events of 2017’s Blade Runner 2049. The science-fiction limited series stars Schafer as Cora, a human fugitive posing as a Blade Runner, alongside Michelle Yeoh as Olwen, an aging Blade Runner facing death.

#31354. The Story Behind Peggy Scott’s Wedding Dress

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1711 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

The Story Behind Peggy Scott’s Wedding Dress

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor.
  • It’s 88 degrees on a humid June day in Troy, Newly introduced York, and Denée Benton stands in a local church’s outbuilding, posing in Peggy Scott’s wedding dress, not breaking a sweat.
  • It has been revealed that it has been a long, hot day of filming, and the cast and crew are scheduled to keep going for many more hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

It’s 88 degrees on a humid June day in Troy, Newly introduced York, and Denée Benton stands in a local church’s outbuilding, posing in Peggy Scott’s wedding dress, not breaking a sweat.

It has been revealed that it has been a long, hot day of filming, and the cast and crew are scheduled to keep going for many more hours. To get to this photo shoot, I had to walk past a cramped church hallway where Cynthia Nixon, Audra McDonald, and John Douglas Thompson sat together in various stages of Gilded Age undress, trading inside jokes. Everyone on set is in a state of elation, both because of the long-planned-for episode featuring the wedding of Peggy and Dr. William Kirkland and because it’s the day of Game 4 of the Knicks’s historic NBA run. A few hours after I leave set, Nixon will post a reel of the cast reacting to the Knicks win in their Gilded Age finery. But even amidst all of this excitement, Benton in her wedding dress steals the show.

In a recent development, writers, production assistants, costume designers, and even Jordan Donica, who plays Dr. Kirkland, gather to watch the shoot. Benton, in the middle of it all, is poised in the gown of white lace, a corset underneath, dress lines crisp, makeup unsmudged, a picture of bridal serenity. Later, Kasia Walicka Maimone, the show’s costume designer, will tell me she spied Benton doing breathing exercises in the church pews, just to maintain her stamina.

Industry observers note that peggy has been a fan favorite since her introduction in the show’s first episode. An ambitious, upper-class Black woman in Gilded Age America, she is an anomaly in period television. Her storyline has introduced viewers to the world of the Black elite, a burgeoning class that emerged during Reconstruction and would dominate Black political and cultural life to the present day. Popular nonfiction books like Our Kind of People have documented the history of this group, but they have been largely absent from television. Even Black weddings, of any time period, are rarely portrayed on American TV. So how do you design a dress for a wedding that hasn’t been seen before?

It has been revealed that “The Gilded Age,” as the period between the 1870s and 1890s is known, “was famous for its excitement [around fashion],” says Walicka Maimone. “How do we represent this excitement? How do we pull out from the historical research things that we, the modern audience, are going to be excited about? We have this giant library of about 50 to 60,000 images that we’ve collected since season 1 … but there’s always manipulation that I apply to it.” Peggy’s wedding dress “resonates with a lot of elements from the period, but it’s not a direct quote of any one specific dress.…What was really important to both Denée and me was the composite of the silhouette [and] the texture of the lace,” a detail that was “referred to in the script directly by her mother-in-law.”.

“The speed that we had to accomplish the design and execution and put it on the screen was astronomical,” Walicka Maimone says. “Hundreds of hands altogether contribute to the making. Each dress takes about six to eight weeks to be built.” Those working on the final bridal look included the in-house costume-design team, milliners for the veil and hat, a jeweler in Rome who designed Peggy’s earrings, and on-set tailors who maintained the costume during filming.

“My wedding dress had over 75 buttons going down the back. Amber, my head dresser, buttoned each one by hand. The craftsmanship was really unbelievable,” Benton tells me a few months later. “It felt powerful to me, spiritually. It felt like we were embodying a moment for a lot of people. I have never seen a luxury Black wedding of the 1800s on any screen, on a stage, in any popular media. And so it really feels like we’re getting to be a part of a pop-culture history moment.”.

Peggy is a child of post-Reconstruction America. Her father, Arthur, experienced enslavement, but she is part of the first generation of Black people born into freedom and citizenship. The thrill of watching her on screen is seeing a character who relishes pushing against the boundaries of what that might mean. She is both an avatar of modern viewers’ desires and a fantasy of what Black womanhood might have looked like in a time of dynamic social change and fabulous dressing. For Peggy, the question of a wedding and marriage takes on additional significance.

According to recent reports, “Because the law of the land during enslavement recognized enslaved people as property, [and] therefore not protected by the law, nor were there unions, whether they were chosen unions or forced unions … they could be separated at any moment. The law did not protect the sanctity of marriage for Black people, for enslaved people,” explains historian Erica Armstrong Dunbar, who is chair of the African-American Studies department at Emory University, in addition to a consultant on The Gilded Age.

Marriage for the Gilded Age generation of Black people was an assertion of agency and an act of claiming Black humanity. The ability to choose partners and form Black families—and have those family bonds legally protected—was a radical act in the aftermath of slavery. All of this history can inform the context of Peggy Scott’s marriage, but what that wedding might look like on screen is another question.

Industry observers note that “When we first started talking about the season and the wedding, Sonja Warfield [the episode’s writer] and Julian Fellowes [The Gilded Age’s creator] were very invested in the notion of the jumping of the broom and that being a part of African American wedding tradition,” Armstrong Dunbar explains. Jumping the broom was a wedding tradition practiced by some enslaved people, a ceremonial act to mark a bond that by definition was not legally recognized.

Sources indicate that “I immediately was like, but that’s not really happening in the 1880s,” Armstrong Dunbar explains. “People were actually distancing themselves from many of the traditional experiences connected to the weddings of enslaved people.”.

In a recent development, fellowes, Warfield, and Gilded Age executive producer Salli Richardson-Whitfield and producer Davita Scarlett, however, were all adamant about including this practice in the wedding episode. Many of them had participated in broom-jumping ceremonies in their own weddings; the practice became popular again in the 1970s, ’80s, and ’90s as post–Civil Rights era couples looked to include specifically African American rituals in their wedding ceremonies.

But part of the pleasure of The Gilded Age is watching how the show plays with historical conventions and anachronisms to further draw viewers into characters’ lives. In this case, the writers and producers decided to give Peggy’s father, Arthur, who was once enslaved, the task of handing the broom he used in his wedding ceremony to his daughter, a moment that recognizes the family’s beginnings and its triumph of seeing a freeborn daughter legally wed. “It really encapsulated the way in which people try to meld traditions when they’re bringing their families together,” says Scarlett. “It just felt too delicious and too interesting and too thematically rich to pass up.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I knew that we were going to be doing Peggy getting married, and I claimed it. I mentioned, ‘No one else is allowed to direct this wedding but me,’ ” says director Richardson-Whitfield. “I just wanted to make sure that it was as lush and gorgeous and special as anything else that we’ve done on the show.”.

This included the decision to feature a gospel choir. “We specifically chose also to do it a cappella and not have any instruments with the music because I felt like those beautiful Black voices were enough to fill the church,” she says. An a cappella chorus singing spirituals would have been, like the broom jumping, frowned upon by many upper-class Black people in the 1880s, but that tension provided another opportunity to deepen the wedding scenes. “Just because we are African American people doesn’t mean we all think the same thing,” Richardson-Whitfield says. “It’s nice to be able to explore different kinds of Black people.”.

The show’s commitment to nuance and its willingness to acknowledge the historical existence of different kinds of marginalized people means its fan base stretches far and wide. Recently, the creative agency Little Significant World hosted a Gilded Age drag ball and panel on queer black history with Benton, activist and Gilded Age fan Brittany Packnett Cunningham, and queer historian Hugh Ryan. The event was packed.

In a recent development, “I think that people see Peggy as this sort of doll princess,” Benton tells me, “but as the actor playing her … bell hooks has this quote that’s like, ‘Queer not as in who I sleep with, but queer as in at odds with everything around me.’ That is Peggy. Period. There was not really a class of professional women [during the Gilded Age]; you were either aristocracy or you were working class. And then to be a Black professional, she really is one of one moving through this space in her time. And I find that to be very queer.”.

“That’s one of the two powers of history work for me,” claims Ryan. “One is seeing … ‘Oh, things actually were really different back then. So that means they could be really different in the future.’ And I think that's liberatory. But the other part, and this is where I think The Gilded Age shines … is getting people excited. I was in a panel with 60 Black queer folk in a Black queer space in Bed-Stuy talking about the Gilded Age and Black drag kings in vaudeville. That conversation only happens because beautiful art sparks our interest and allows us to see a place in the past.”.

“As an artist, you can’t really ask for more than to do something that is popular and meaningful at the same time,” Benton says. “The sweet spot.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas have made it to the semifinals on Dancing With the Stars, but it’s been a tough week of rehearsals for Maura thanks to a persistent rib injury. Maura opened up about her rib pain last week, and apparently the situation hasn’t improved. In fact, she’s reportedly had to postpone multiple rehearsals this week—including one right before semifinals.

“She reinjured the rib over the weekend and had to postpone another rehearsal and get looked at by medics again,” a source tells The Sun. “She’s trying to give it her all but giving it her all is costing her physically. Her body is hanging on by a thread but she’s more determined than ever to push through.”.

So, will Maura be able to dance in the finals next week (assuming she and Mark score well and get the necessary votes)? She plans to push through.

Sources indicate that “She knows after this dance she only has one more week left and she thinks she can do it,” notes the insider. “So she’s still in it to win it. She wants it for herself but I think she wants the trophy for Mark even more because she knows how much it would mean to him and they’ve gotten so close this past year. But she does want it for herself, both because she came in not being a dancer and genuinely thinking she’d be an early boot so getting this far would mean a ton to her. Plus she knows the career opportunities that would come from it would be incredible.”.

Here’s to hoping Maura gets a chance to rest and heal between episodes!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I spent much of Thursday staring at photographs of Jensen Huang’s shoes arranged in one soldierly line longer in both directions than the frame could hold.
  • This is a philosophy I share with Jensen, and my version saves even more time and energy: Don’t change clothes.
  • In a recent development, in Jensen’s case, there’s no mystery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I spent much of Thursday staring at photographs of Jensen Huang’s shoes arranged in one soldierly line longer in both directions than the frame could hold. These dozen pairs—each different, all dazzling—were but a glimpse of his footwear armies. Jensen’s Hermès slip-ons and dozens of black leather jackets are not only his fashion signatures; they’re also proof of his decision to not waste precious energy deciding what clothes to wear each morning.

This is a philosophy I share with Jensen, and my version saves even more time and energy: Don’t change clothes. But I like men’s shoes, I’ve sold men’s shoes, and I believe that a man’s shoes reveal facets of his public persona and private desires.

In a recent development, in Jensen’s case, there’s no mystery. He’s a brilliant guy who was once a small, smart immigrant kid bullied and beaten at a Kentucky Baptist reform school that his uncle mistook for a boarding school. Now he’s 63, a five-foot-six AI titan standing in adorable—size 9 is my guess—multi-thousand-dollar slip-ons atop his $140 billion, with his dick out and dripping all over his kicks du jour.

And we are left to sort the tragedy, seek catharsis, and remind ourselves again—and again—that Jensen Huang’s downfall awaits any man who ignores the fundamental law of our own animal nature: Ven der putz shteht, der sechel licht in drert: When the penis stands, the brain goes to hell.

Recent findings suggest that I make no moral judgment here; we have no basis or right to do so. The college sweetheart he married 41 years ago, along with their two grown children, are the only souls with standing in this case. But I think it’s only fair, in light of current reporting on Jensen’s three concurrent affairs—that’s two side pieces plus Princess Honey-Pot plus a wife—to reconsider that vast battalion of decision-saving slip-ons and what it indicates.

Industry observers note that the shoes reveal a man with smallish feet whose penis was too busy making decisions to consider laces, love, or the welfare of his family and business. And there aren’t enough shoes, dollars, or women in the world to fill the hole in Jensen Huang.

Industry observers note that the Latin word ‘invidia’ means envy. This, given Jensen’s shoes, is not coincidence or irony; it’s a weakling’s shamed confession. Hermes needs to cobble one last pair for Jensen Huang, long, bright red, and floppy.

  • Industry observers note that kylie Jenner notably skipped the red carpet at the Governors Awards last night, leaving boyfriend Timothée Chalamet to walk it solo.
  • Industry observers note that once inside, Jenner revealed a stunning vintage Roberto Cavalli gown pulled from the designer’s Fall/Winter 2006 runway collection.
  • Industry observers note that the latest Victoria’s Secret angel wore the dress with a pretty, elegant blowout and a lined pink lip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that kylie Jenner notably skipped the red carpet at the Governors Awards last night, leaving boyfriend Timothée Chalamet to walk it solo. But, of course, her gown was well worth the wait.

Industry observers note that once inside, Jenner revealed a stunning vintage Roberto Cavalli gown pulled from the designer’s Fall/Winter 2006 runway collection. The rare design came in a silky champagne satin, with tiny sleeves and a crisscrossing back. Little crystals and gems embellished parts of the gown, while a subtle floral print adorned it. As Jenner walked, a romantic train trailed behind her.

Industry observers note that the latest Victoria’s Secret angel wore the dress with a pretty, elegant blowout and a lined pink lip. She shared a photo of the look on her Instagram, but did not grace us with snaps of herself with Chalamet at the ceremony. Maybe one day.

The Dune: Part Three star was dapper in a classic black tuxedo from Giorgio Armani.

Photos and videos shared on social media show the two holding hands inside, as well as Jenner chatting with fellow guests, such as Penélope Cruz.

Since they began dating in early 2023, Jenner has accompanied Chalamet to many a starry red-carpet event. They made their striking red-carpet debut at the 70th David di Donatello awards in Rome, Italy, in May 2025, after having attended the Golden Globes and the Oscars together without walking the carpet. Months later, in December, they made a statement in matching orange Chrome Hearts looks for the red-carpet premiere of the actor’s viral film Marty Supreme in Los Angeles.

It has been revealed that their last joint red-carpet moment was in March 2026, when they attended the Vanity Fair Oscars party. Then, the couple contrasted in black and white looks, with Jenner wearing a body-hugging McQueen gown covered in inky beads, and Chalamet going for an icy Givenchy suit.

We can’t get enough of these two, and it seems they can’t get enough of each other.

Los Angeles has no shortage of awards demonstrates, but ELLE’s annual Women in Hollywood event has always been about something more: putting the spotlight on the women whose work makes the industry worth watching. On Monday night, eight of film and television’s most talked-about talents came together to celebrate their collective achievements, with plenty of oohs, aahs, and well-deserved gushes along the way.

This year’s honorees—Carrie Coon, Elizabeth Debicki, Rosalind Eleazar, Julianne Moore, Samantha Morton, Inde Navarrette, Florence Pugh, and Penélope Cruz—gathered at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills for an evening hosted by ELLE editor-in-chief Nina Garcia.

Presented in partnership with Ralph Lauren and Bulgari, with support from Evian, the soirée drew familiar faces from across Tinseltown. Matt Damon, Seth Rogen, Bryce Dallas Howard, Alexander Skarsgård, and Louisa Jacobson were among those who took the stage to present the honors, while Morton accepted hers remotely from her home in London, where she was sick with the flu.

Beyond the eight honorees, the guest list included Lily James, Ashley Park, Elsa Hosk, Madison Beer, Jackie Tohn, Molly Sims, and more.

Champagne and yuzu mocktails flowed as guests mingled before making their way into the ballroom, where a three-course dinner awaited: beet salad, Chilean sea bass, and chocolate tortino.

Garcia kicked things off by celebrating a banner year for moviegoing, while reminding the room that there’s still work to be done when it comes to creating opportunities for women. “We need roles for women that are messy, complicated, funny, and real—and sometimes even older than 50!” she remarked.

She pointed to the eight honorees as a reminder of what’s possible when those roles make it to the screen. “You are all proof of what happens when these roles are written—you knock it out of the park. These women we are honoring? The characters they have played? They are not decorative. They’re not supporting a man’s journey. They are women in full.”.

Is This the Greatest Fashion Auction of All Time?

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that who owns four vintage Dior Maasai necklaces?
  • Sources indicate that dubbed the Infinite Wardrobe, the multipart auction contains haute couture, ready-to-wear, handbags, and accessories from the likes of Chanel, Dior, Hermès, Valentino, Roberto Cavalli, Fendi, and Ungaro.
  • It has been revealed that much of the Infinite Wardrobe is unworn or only worn once, pristinely preserved like a time capsule for decades in one closet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that who owns four vintage Dior Maasai necklaces? Not very many people, except for, of course, one of Paris’s most mysterious women and deeply devoted collectors of fashion. The anonymous French clotheshorse is now the subject of an upcoming multipart, 3,000-piece sale at Maurice Auction. “It’s not someone who is known by the industry, it’s just someone who was very wealthy and that could afford such a collection as a true and passionate collector for more than 30 years,” Salomé Pirson, co-founder of Maurice Auction, tells ELLE.

Sources indicate that dubbed the Infinite Wardrobe, the multipart auction contains haute couture, ready-to-wear, handbags, and accessories from the likes of Chanel, Dior, Hermès, Valentino, Roberto Cavalli, Fendi, and Ungaro. The Infinite Wardrobe will kick off with a live auction on November 18 in Paris, followed by eight different online-only auctions sorted by brand or subject (Chanel, Italian fashion, Dior, bags, for instance). Even with the growing interest in auctions recently spurred by a younger demographic, it’s certainly one of the most extensive fashion auctions that has happened in recent years. Earlier this year, Maurice Auction broke records when it sold rare haute couture from the collection of couture queen Mouna Ayoub.

It has been revealed that much of the Infinite Wardrobe is unworn or only worn once, pristinely preserved like a time capsule for decades in one closet. Some of it even still has tags attached. “What’s unusual is the volume,” indicates Marie-Laurence Tixier, co-founder of Maurice Auction. “The client was really someone who collected, and when she liked a look or a pair of shoes, she would buy all the colors.” For the auction, that means Hermès Oran sandals in every shade of the rainbow and every iteration of vintage Chanel Gripoix necklaces. Some of the items will be sold in more than a dozen variations.

When the duo first encountered the collection, it was stored in a single Parisian apartment, all exhibited by color, type of accessory, and brand. “I’ve heard that people, when they went to have dinner at her place, they visited the closet, because it was a piece of art itself,” adds Tixier. It’s by far the biggest auction the company has ever done since it was founded in 2022, and also the biggest undertaking of their careers in terms of cataloging, researching, and organizing all of the pieces. “It’s like going into a fantasy closet where you realize it’s not gonna be a dream, it’s gonna be a real job for three months,” says Tixier. The rarest items were researched in collaboration with Kerry Taylor, fashion’s favorite London auctioneer.

If you love designer fashion, it’s a great opportunity to pick up a vintage luxury just before the holidays. But for the real fashion freaks, there are some ultra-rare gems that rarely come to market, too. Think: Jean Paul Gaultier-designed Hermès crocodile jackets, Emanuel Ungaro haute couture, and incredible, lightweight vintage Fendi furs. “She had exquisite taste, it’s very elegant, very, very refined,” says Tixier. “There are no logos.”.

Recent findings suggest that roberto Cavalli beaded trousers, Christian Dior by Gianfranco Ferré mini bustle dresses, and Gianni Versace embroidered jackets are just a few of the treasures available in the first part of the auction. In other words: the dream closet is real, and soon, it will be up for grabs.

To be honest, movies made in the 1990s are kind of all over the place—but that’s what we loved about the decade. You never knew what to expect, and Christmas and holiday movies were no exception. The decade was filled with a bunch of auteurs making daring choices (a.k.a. everything Tim Burton made, but particularly the movie that's somehow about Halloween and Christmas simultaneously), some insta-classics (Muppet Christmas Carol), and some pretty wild setups that have aged *weirdly* but still give us the nostalgia feels (While You Were Sleeping, Home Alone, The Santa Clause, and a whole bunch more).

Seriously, go back to some of your old faves and remember how we just accepted Arnold Schwarzenegger as a normal salesman from Minnesota (Jingle All the Way). To be even more honest, the '90s production speed couldn't hold a candle to the streaming era. These days, there are hundreds of Christmas movies released across various streaming network every year. We’ve only been able to scrounge up 30ish holiday movies for the whole decade.

In a recent development, beyond the classics you know and love, there are a bunch of movies on here you probably missed the first time around—or haven't watched in actual decades. If you're here because you grew up on '90s movies, allow us to refresh your memory with some underrated classics and tell you where you can watch all your old faves. And, if you're here because you want something different for your holiday-viewing experience because you've already watched Elf 10,000 times, start at the top of this list and work your way down. Happy holiday viewing!

According to recent reports, the Halloween-Christmas crossover no one expected, The Nightmare Before Christmas is a gorgeous stop-motion piece of art that's aged better than anyone expected. Tim Burton is a vocal lover of the holidays (this is the first of two times he'll be on this list), and his deeply weird vision is surprisingly moving—who hasn't felt like Jack Skellington desperately wishing for Christmas but also not totally doing it right?

Industry observers note that christmas movie, or movie that takes place during Christmas? While You Were Sleeping sees Sandra Bullock's Lucy save a man from an oncoming train, but not before he falls into a coma. While unconscious, hijinx ensue, and his family mistakes Lucy for his fiance. A classic '90s rom-com, this basically started a nationwide obsession with Sandra Bullock, Bill Pullman, and falling in love in snowy Chicago.

We realize that there are more beloved Muppet movies out there, but this one is *it* for us. Michael Caine is giving it 110 percent here, which means you get some seriousness alongside the giggles. Also, it contains both the scariest scene (hello, Ghost of Christmas Future) and the most bittersweet scene (hello, Beaker and the scarf) in a Christmas movie ever.

The Christmas movie to end all Christmas movies came to us in 1990. Home Alone follows a kid abandoned by his family on Christmas who must protect his home against two Grinch-like burglars.

According to recent reports, same, same, but different. Home Alone 2 follows the same abandoned kid, this time left adrift in New York City. The film sees the return of our beloved burglars, plus a cameo from a pre-political Donald Trump. Ah, simpler times.

Tim Burton is back, and with a newer, bleaker vision of the holiday season. Like some of its neighbors on this list, Batman Returns is a movie that takes place over the holidays, not a holiday movie. If you want a classic Burton look at the nightmare beauty of Christmas, wrapped in a cat woman suit and a cape, return to this movie during the holiday season.

According to recent reports, praise be! The best-selling gospel album of all time! If you're only familiar with the music, you should absolutely watch this Whitney Houston, Courtney B. Vance, Denzel Washington love triangle Christmas movie, in which Denzel plays a literal angel. If you grew up watching this, you know it's the corny, sweet, heartwarming goodness the holiday needs.

This is...a weird movie, and not just because it features the message that Christmas is all about buying sh*t you don't need. Arnold Schwarzenegger is...improbably cast as a frustrated mattress salesman from Minneapolis, and it only gets weirder from there. But if you're watching it for the nostalgia factor or just to remember how wild it really was, go for it!

In a recent development, nothing indicates the '90s like Jonathan Taylor Thomas, heartthrob of millions of teen girls. This admittedly out-there premise features JTT as a noncommittal boarding school teen whose dad promises him a Porsche - if he makes it home in time for Christmas dinner. A weird, wacky road trip ensues (and life lessons are learned, obv).

Recent findings suggest that if you loved the Olsen twins, this was probably a repeat watch in your house (guilty as charged). It's a deeply '90s TV movie that—fun fact—was the first time they ever portrayed separate characters. This one's a wild ride, quite literally, as the kiddos are just trying to get to grandma's and instead go on a bunch of adventures in a delivery truck. Just go with it, it's sweet.

In a recent development, this movie is a pretty obvious attempt to capture the magic of the original - which came out in 1988, so it unfortunately doesn't make the list. It's also basically the same movie in an airport. But it's still fun to watch Bruce Willis grumble, "Just once, I’d like a regular, normal Christmas" to himself while getting into a bunch of action shenanigans.

This is another action movie that didn't *have* to be set around Christmas—but it's more fun that way. Geena Davis is the coolest as a suburban housewife with amnesia. who turns out to be a hardcore assassin, alongside Samuel L. Jackson. This movie has an improbably happy ending, which, if that doesn't make it a Christmas movie, we don't know what does!

Industry observers note that this early Nora Ephron film is absolute chaos (which is probably why you've never heard of it), but you can't beat the star-studded cast of Steve Martin, Rita Wilson, Rob Reiner, and Adam Sandler, just to name a few. And they're doing all the slapstick simultaneously, which will at least make for an entertaining hour and a half.

Did you know there was a direct-to-video Beauty and the Beast holiday special? Because we sure didn't. But, basically, it takes place in the middle of the first movie, where the Beast hates Christmas (and joy, apparently), and Belle has to convince him to let the holiday spirit into his heart. Light holiday fluff right this way!

In a recent development, the last "newly introduced" Peanuts special to air on CBS, over nine million households watched this—but it's also not as popular (or well-known) as the original 1960s Charlie Brown special. If you're hoping for more Peanuts content this holiday season and haven't watched this in a long time (or ever), this one's gonna hit you right in the feels.

All hail our queen Julie Andrews! This TV movie is making the correct choice by letting James Garner's character fall in love with her—the premise being that two strangers take shelter together during a winter storm. Corny, manufactured drama and romance ensue. If you happen to like Hallmark movies, this is an early draft of the romances you know and love.

Industry observers note that this movie kinda requires you to watch the first films in the three-part series and also...is not a great movie. But John Travolta and Kirstie Alley are trying their very best to make it work—and if you ever wanted to listen to Diane Keaton and Danny DeVito do the voices for two strange dog characters, then do we have the movie for you.

Sources indicate that dated in a kinda gross way? You bet. The protagonist kills Santa and that's not even the weirdest part. The Santa Clause is an important part of our childhood, if you grew up in the '90s. Maybe fast-forward to the fun, sweet parts and skip the fatphobia and problematic co-parenting!

Sources indicate that not technically ’90s, but spiritually very ’90s. This is Tim Allen in his peak family-comedy era, cozy suburban Christmas aesthetics, early-mall-culture whimsy, and that iconic red-sweater warmth that defined an entire generation’s holiday TV rotation.

Sources indicate that the '90s gave us a theatrical remake of the 1947 classic of the same name, this time starring Richard Attenborough as Santa (spoiler alert). Fun fact about this film: it premiered at Radio City Music Hall, featuring a Rockettes number and a performance from Kenny G.

With boot season in full force, we’re finding out just how versatile they really are. A pair can instantly make an outfit feel more thoughtful and elevated, bringing polish and structure to an everyday look. Pair that with the season’s snakeskin trend, and you’ve found a true statement piece.

Found in an array of neutral hues and styles, snakeskin boots are the secret neutral your wardrobe might be missing. The trend translates from chic to sophisticated to downright edgy, no matter the silhouette.

Sources indicate that for an easy way to wear the look, style them with denim and a classic knit for a casual weekend outfit, or let them anchor a tailored dress or midi skirt for evening. Either way, the texture does the talking, so keep the rest of your outfit simple and let your boots take center stage.

Below, we’ve rounded up some of the best snakeskin boots to shop now.

The brown snakeskin boots we didn’t know we needed. This style features a shaft that can be worn gathered or straight, adding versatility to a pointed toe and sleek kitten heel. Wear them with your favorite knit minidress or midi skirt.

This snakeskin ankle boot features an understated cap toe, adding more depth and personality to any outfit. Wear it with cropped denim or a slip skirt for an easy, elevated look.

In a recent development, this tall, over-the-knee silhouette is the kind you’ll want to build your looks around. The natural sand colorway adds warmth to the season’s rich color palette and pairs perfectly with burgundy, brown, hunter green, and more of fall’s favorite hues.

It has been revealed that this burgundy iteration by Rabanne is worth celebrating. It adds instant edge and glamour to jeans and a tee, and the silver-tone metal toe caps engraved with the brand’s logo make it a true statement piece. Keep the rest of your look simple and let the details do the talking.

These butter yellow snakeskin boots are the perfect transitional pick, whether you’re going from summer to fall or winter to spring. The flat heel makes them a top candidate for an everyday go-to.

A snakeskin Chelsea boot pairs sophistication with practicality, thanks to a chunky heel and elastic side gores. This style reads polished with a dose of cool-girl energy.

Industry observers note that this all-black snake-embossed pair leans into the trend with a softer yet no less impactful take. The tonal finish keeps the look sleek and easy to style, whether you’re dressing up a pair of barrel jeans or adding edge to a slip dress.

According to recent reports, this classic black-and-white snake print stands out against the darker shades of fall and winter. Pair it with neutral knits or tailored basics to let the pattern be the focal point of your look.

Styled with dressy trousers or denim alike, the Lennon Boots, inspired by the Beatles, merge an elongated toe with a Cuban heel for elevated everyday dressing.

Recent findings suggest that these knee-high boots hug the leg, making them a perfect match for all your ’90s rom-com-inspired outfits. Think cozy knits, plaid skirts, and a little bit of main-character energy.

With a subtle angled heel and a tall shaft, these snakeskin boots have an extra dose of personality. The textured finish adds depth to neutral outfits, such as an LBD, without feeling over the top.

#31315. The Best Greens Supplements to Boost Energy, Gut Health, and Skin

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1460 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

The Best Greens Supplements to Boost Energy, Gut Health, and Skin

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1460 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that with the wellness industry still booming, we’re inundated with products and devices that promise a shortcut to total health.
  • One supplement class that continues to reign in the mainstream is greens powders, more than just green juice in powder form.
  • Sources indicate that these supercharged green food powders aren’t just specialty items at vitamin shops; you can now find them everywhere—from drugstores to Amazon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that with the wellness industry still booming, we’re inundated with products and devices that promise a shortcut to total health. Now, there’s a long list of gadgets, apps, topical creams, and ingestible supplements designed to clear your mind, calm your nervous system, boost energy, and improve sleep.

One supplement class that continues to reign in the mainstream is greens powders, more than just green juice in powder form. Below, the experts unpack everything you really need to know about the new generation of greens supplements.

Sources indicate that these supercharged green food powders aren’t just specialty items at vitamin shops; you can now find them everywhere—from drugstores to Amazon. But according to Philippa May, co-founder of women-first greens powder brand Naere, the major players have one glaring problem: they’re created by men, for men.

Recent findings suggest that “We created Nectar 01 as an antidote to the male-dominated market,” she indicates. “The highly successful green powders already in the category were built around male-focused language: performance, optimization, stronger. And supplements aimed at women often leaned into insecurities: de-bloat, anti-aging, fixing your skin, helping you ‘bounce back.’ We felt there was nothing truly speaking to women as they are, beyond problems to be solved, and instead as modern individuals navigating the natural flux of daily life, in need of support rather than correction.”.

Industry observers note that this is where the next generation of greens powders comes in. Sitting alongside Naere is the much-hyped LymaID²: the biohacking superbrand’s latest launch (and its most accessibly priced offering, too). Founder Lucy Goff enlists the most revered specialists in a field to power her revolutionary introduces, so she created ID² in collaboration with Professor Paul Clayton, a clinical pharmacologist and senior scientific adviser to the U.K. government.

Similarly, Catherine Hurley has focused on organic powdered fruits and vegetables, rather than a long list of trendy ingredients that may appeal to the world’s biohacking bros. Her Newroad 30 powder contains a megadose of polyphenol-rich fruits and berries, alongside vegetables and pulses to support the gut microbiome. In short, it’s not a hack for superhuman fitness, but a real-food supplement to boost your existing diet.

It has been revealed that most of these powders contain greens—from common produce like spinach and kale to specialty greens like alfalfa grass and chlorophyll. These powders often also include fiber-rich foods, probiotic sources, and digestive enzymes to help further reduce bloating.

According to recent reports, but what do the experts really think? Nutritionists largely agree that greens powders can support wellness, but only when paired with a healthy, varied diet. (If your core food groups are Pret sandwiches and cortisol, mainlining a glass of greens each morning won’t save you.).

“The starting point for me is always food,” says Jessica Shand, a naturopathic nutritionist and author of The Hormone Balance Handbook. “No powder will ever replace the benefits of eating a wide variety of vegetables, fruit, legumes, nuts, and seeds because whole foods provide so much more than individual vitamins and minerals alone. They contain fiber, polyphenols, phytonutrients, and thousands of interactions that we simply cannot fully replicate in a supplement,” she says.

That said, we also have to be realistic about how people live. “Busy schedules, frequent travel, limited access to fresh produce, or simply not consuming enough plant variety are all situations where a greens or plant powder may be helpful,” Shand adds. “However, I would only ever recommend a high-quality product, and, in my opinion, those are relatively few and far between.”.

So, which greens powders are really worth investing in? Below, see the Bazaar breakdown of the supplements to stick to this year, all editor-tested.

Lyma is a brand known for moving the goalposts with its innovative (albeit investment-level) products, and ID²—the brand’s probiotic powdered supplement—is no different.

It has been revealed that “The modern diet leaves most of us less than what we could be,” notes Paul Clayton, a professor who worked with the brand on the launch. “Lyma ID² was built to put those elements back into place—the ones that the science of the longest-living people in human history told us matter most.”.

Based on the philosophy that longevity begins with a healthy gut, ID² contains a diverse range of prebiotic fibers, since no single strain benefits every section of the gut, along with bioavailable omega-3s and a range of minerals and vitamins.

Personally, I saw a huge difference after drinking the formula religiously for six weeks, especially with bloating. By the one-month mark, my midafternoon brain fog had all but subsided. And thanks to the genuinely pleasant grapefruit taste, I’ve stuck with it for several months now.

Newroad 30 is a gut supplement containing 30 organic powdered fruits and vegetables. Rather than focusing on greens, which can be an acquired taste, founder Catherine Hurley has placed red fruits and berries at the center of her formula. “They provide a rich source of polyphenols and antioxidants that support gut health, skin health, and healthy aging,” she explains. “We still include vegetables and pulses, but their flavors sit behind the berry profile. The result is a product that delivers the benefits while tasting genuinely great, making it much easier to enjoy every day.” Indeed, if you’ve struggled to commit to an earthy greens powder before, this black-currant-tinged powder is the one to choose, delivering vitamins and minerals to support a healthy gut microbiome without the unpleasant taste.

In a recent development, another benefit is how Newroad 30 is made. “We freeze-dry every ingredient. Most powders are spray-dried, and this method doesn’t preserve nutrients, fiber, and polyphenols as well as freeze-drying, which also preserves flavor,” claims Hurley. Everything is organic here, too—an key consideration because, as Hurley explains, “the process of drying the ingredients concentrates any pesticides present.”.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, what’s not in this plant-powered powder is as crucial as what is. “I would not want to take a powder with additives, such as sweeteners, flavorings, colors, emulsifiers, and binders,” Hurley adds, and Newroad 30 is free of them.

One of the longstanding powdered supplements on the market, Elle Macpherson’s The Super Elixir Daily Greens is particularly beneficial for those navigating hormonal shifts, such as perimenopause. Alongside prebiotics, four probiotic strains, adaptogenic botanicals, and powdered greens, it includes a cocktail of vitamins and minerals—from ginseng and glutamine to B vitamins—designed to boost energy and reduce brain fog. For the skin challenges that often come at this time (think: loss of laxity and dryness), it also includes biotin and zinc.

While this power cocktail won’t directly balance your hormones, it will provide a strong nutritional foundation to support the body through such a seismic shift. The taste is distinctly “green” (if you’re picky about flavor, expect a challenge), but the energy-boosting potential is real.

The original green powder, AG1, was made with athletes in mind but is for anyone who needs extra physical energy and mental clarity. Essentially, it’s a potent, well-rounded multivitamin that provides 100 percent of the RDA for key nutrients, including vitamins C and E, energy-providing B vitamins, two strains of gut-boosting probiotics, plant superfoods, and stress-reducing adaptogens.

Anecdotal praise for this one isn’t hard to find: Chances are, you already know one loyal devotee. However, the formula notably lacks iron, which, since women generally need more iron than men, points to the brand’s male-leaning marketing. Also, keep in mind the formula is a proprietary blend, so the brand doesn’t disclose the exact amount of each ingredient.

Built by women, for women, Naere brings ingredient transparency to the supplements space with its online Integrity Index™—a digital service that analyzes any supplement, from any brand, and delivers a detailed breakdown of its safety and efficacy based on your personal needs.

This uncompromising focus on quality over quantity naturally follows through into its debut launch, Nectar 01. This powdered supplement contains 30 ingredients—four of which are patented—significantly fewer than many competitors.

You can delve into every ingredient on the brand’s website, but the headliners are marine-derived hydrolyzed collagen peptides and sodium hyaluronate to support skin and joints; algae-derived astaxanthin for antioxidant protection; selenium for immune function; and a patented black pepper extract to improve the bioavailability of the other ingredients.

Recent findings suggest that “Ultimately, the best supplements aren’t about including everything, but about choosing well-dosed, bioavailable ingredients that genuinely deliver,” claims co-founder Philippa May. “And most importantly, consistency always wins. One supplement you take daily will always beat the supplement stack you forget.”.

Industry observers note that this is another one I found easy to stick to. The slightly sweet, green taste is peculiar but not unpleasant, and after finishing my first package, I saw real improvements in my bloating and digestion, plus steadier energy levels.

  • In a recent development, fans expressed grave concern for her well-being, questioning whether she should be performing at all.
  • It has been revealed that and there’s another relevant context: With Manon and Sophia already on hiatus, Megan’s absence would leave the group with just three members, only half their original formation of six, and for that reason the group had already postponed three shows.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, online debates about celebrity work culture sparked when KATSEYE’s Megan Skindiel, who is recovering from a concussion, recently performed seated and in sunglasses during a show in Austin on the group’s WILDWORLD Tour. The next night in Dallas, video surfaced of the artist taking part in the group’s intense dance choreography, while wearing what many speculate to be a heart monitor.

In a recent development, fans expressed grave concern for her well-being, questioning whether she should be performing at all. While it is notable to note that we don’t actually know whether it was Megan’s own decision to perform, many still accused KATSEYE’s label, HYBE x Geffen Records, of potentially overworking their artists at the expense of their health. The label is a partnership between the South Korean entertainment company HYBE (home to groups like BTS, Illit, TXT, and Seventeen) and the American label Geffen Records (home to artists such as Olivia Rodrigo, Selena Gomez, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey).

It has been revealed that and there’s another relevant context: With Manon and Sophia already on hiatus, Megan’s absence would leave the group with just three members, only half their original formation of six, and for that reason the group had already postponed three shows. As of now, neither the label nor the group has publicly addressed the criticism.

For longtime K-pop fans, none of this is entirely shocking. Those who follow the industry have most likely already witnessed their idols push through panic attacks, fainting spells, extreme sleep deprivation, injuries from falls, and many other mental and physical struggles in order to give their fans the concert experience they were promised. But for many Western fans, this may be the first look at the grueling expectations that the K-pop world has for its artists, which helps explain the intense concern in their reactions.

Sources indicate that KATSEYE is an especially interesting case for us to explore this friction. The group was formed through Dream Academy, a survival competition run by HYBE and Geffen Records, where the finalists trained mainly in Los Angeles, with trips to HYBE’s headquarters in Seoul. While KATSEYE’s music is mostly in English, the group promotes in both the U.S. and South Korea, exemplifying the group’s unique positioning between the two music industries, each with its own set of rules and ideas of what a pop career demands.

According to recent reports, commercially, that meeting point keeps getting closer, with the dramatic rise of K-pop’s popularity and its growing presence in mainstream Western media. And that cross-cultural exchange is reflected in the music itself: English words increasingly make up the majority of the lyrics in K-pop songs, and many labels are now intentionally debuting members who are proficient in English.

It also helps to compare how music careers get built, starting with how the artists are even first discovered by the world. Many of the West’s biggest stars began as those who were organically noticed: Justin Bieber was discovered through cover videos on YouTube, and Taylor Swift was spotted as a teenager playing Nashville’s Bluebird Cafe. K-pop runs on a completely different model: one where the tech giant trains the individual into being an artist through a strict, meticulous formula within a larger system of strategic control.

Those who make it through the company’s insanely competitive rounds of auditions will then spend years as trainees with no guarantee of debuting. Those years typically involve regular evaluations, private lessons, as well as sometimes group living for management and surveillance purposes. Trainees often agree to be prescribed diet plans and sometimes even cosmetic surgery, as well as close monitoring of their private lives including harsh restrictions on dating and phone use to ensure that their status as trainees remains a secret. And what may be even more jarring for those new to this culture is that many of these trainees are often as young as 13, with more and more labels debuting their idols before they are even close to being legal adults.

Industry observers note that in exchange comes a carefully engineered shot at success, with executives and experts calibrating the exact combination of members, visual concept, songs, and more to optimize audience appeal. Audiences got a glimpse of this process during Dream Academy, though in a more Westernized version. Whatever ethical questions this process raises, it works, at least commercially. All the biggest K-pop groups have come out of this exact system, and the labels continue to stay closely involved throughout their careers.

Industry observers note that but the label isn’t the only relationship that heavily shapes a K-pop artist’s life. There’s also the one with the fans. Western audiences are no strangers to fan culture, from Beatlemania to Swifties, and plenty of domestic K-pop fandoms have a U.S. counterpart. However, one notable cultural difference is one of degree. Take whatever you’ve seen from American fandoms and multiply it by a hundred, and you start to approach the level of devotion an average K-pop stan extends to their bias, or favorite member. They follow idols to concert after concert and every public appearance in between, and they also work together, using step-by-step guides to stream songs in ways that send them up the charts, sometimes even outperforming many mainstream Western artists on global charts like the Billboard Hot 100.

Sources indicate that and that kind of devotion comes with expectations. Many groups have dedicated fan-chatting apps, such as HYBE’s Weverse and the subscription-based Bubble, where artists can post and chat with fans almost directly, and fans come to expect regular contact through this service. Idols are also expected to keep up a cheerful image, to avoid canceling a show that fans paid for at all costs, and to immediately apologize when they fall short, even when the reason is an injury.

Sources indicate that public dating, meanwhile, has long been treated as a career-threatening betrayal for these artists. In 2024, after aespa’s Karina was revealed to be dating an actor, she faced a wave of backlash, causing her to post a handwritten apology to fans. Norms have loosened for established stars, but newcomers, or what the industry calls shin-ins, are discouraged, or often barred from it, by both their companies and their fans.

Industry observers note that because they’re still largely construed as Western artists, KATSEYE is, to a large degree, exempt from these rules. For example, members have been comparatively open about their dating lives—a luxury a Korea-based group would most likely not be afforded. But KATSEYE is still managed by a K-pop company, trained by a K-pop system. It wouldn’t be surprising that some of that ethos of always putting the fans first is internalized within the group’s own decision-making, shaping how much they feel they owe their fans in ways a Western artist might not.

According to recent reports, from a Western perspective, it makes sense why all of this might feel like an oppressive system that needs reform, or even dismantling. And the criticism exists internally as well: On November 16, South Korea’s Culture Ministry officially confirmed the launch of a comprehensive survey to review concerns over young performers’ working conditions following the NewJeans controversy. However, one could argue that Western criticism can often be translated by domestic fans as a kind of white-savior complex, with “outsiders” interfering in the methods and systems that have existed without their attention for decades, while deciding it must assimilate to their terms and standards. Especially when many of these critics lack the necessary understanding of the complicated nuances of how K-pop’s cultural specificity largely reflects South Korea’s distinct historical, political, and socioeconomic landscape—one that dramatically differs from the U.S.

It has been revealed that these aspects of K-pop are deeply normalized within the industry itself: Trainee systems are shown openly in documentaries and TV series, including ones the companies themselves help produce, and artists often talk about those years candidly, suggesting that many of them may not see these practices as the problem outsiders do. And maybe there is also a truth in the idea that K-pop’s impressive commercial success is partly a product of the very controls critics object to, including the symbiotic relationships between artists and their labels, and between artists and their fans. Without that culture, we would probably not have what we now know to be BLACKPINK or BTS.

None of this makes the overworking of artists acceptable, nor does it erase much of the valid concern so many people feel. We are allowed to worry when our favorite artist seems to be pushed too far, whether it’s by their own drive, their label’s instructions, or by the weight of fans’ expectations. And we’re allowed to question the very systems that make that possible—in K-pop, in Hollywood, or anywhere else.

Recent findings suggest that but it’s also worth asking what it might mean for a system with decades of independent history—one that grew largely outside Western norms—to navigate a global spotlight (and the equally globalized standards that come with it). Where does cultural context end and basic safety begin? And who gets to decide what “better” looks like, if not the artists living it?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • In a recent development, as we age, there’s seemingly always something fresh to think about, including adjusting your skin care routine to meet your skin’s evolving needs.
  • Over 40, skin has already started to thin, at both the epidermis and dermis levels, explains Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

In a recent development, as we age, there’s seemingly always something fresh to think about, including adjusting your skin care routine to meet your skin’s evolving needs. You may not need to add a bunch of new products to your current regimen, but increased dryness, changes in texture, fine lines, and enlarged pores may require ingredient swaps that your current lineup can’t deliver. The skin care products you used in your 20s and 30s may have worked then, but once you hit 40, your skin may start to need something different. Experts share how to reset your routine for 40+ skin, including the non-negotiables, new ingredients that can have the greatest impact, and what to avoid to keep your maturing skin looking and feeling its best.

Over 40, skin has already started to thin, at both the epidermis and dermis levels, explains Dr. Suzan Obagi, a board-certified dermatologist, associate professor of dermatology and plastic surgery, and director of the UPMC Cosmetic Surgery & Skin Health Center. “This means that skin will start to appear more fragile, fine lines will start to show, and skin becomes drier. For these reasons, a good skin care regimen should include a retinoid (retinol, retinaldehyde, or tretinoin) to help improve skin thickness, increase extracellular matrix proteins (collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)), and encourage fibroblasts to make more of our Natural Moisturizing Factor (NMF),” Obagi tells ELLE.

Most skin over 40 also has some sun damage, which Obagi notes can present as freckles and sun spots. Well before 40 and certainly after, there’s one daily non-negotiable for skin of any age: sunscreen. If the spots have already shown up, Obagi recommends a skin-brightening serum with tranexamic acid (TXA), antioxidants, and peptides to help correct the hyperpigmentation.

Additionally, Dr. Chris Tomassian, a California-based, board-certified dermatologist and founder of The Dermatology Collective, notes a retinol at night will go a long way, as will vitamin C in the morning and aggressive moisturization.

As for ingredients, Tomassian says the key players in the post-40 reset will be retinol, SPF, and vitamin C, as already noted, along with PDRN, ectoin, ceramides, and occasionally estradiol.

If you’re not already on a daytime and nighttime routine, now’s the time to start.

According to recent reports, morning: Use a gentle cleanser if your skin is oily or if you didn’t get to a proper wash the night before. Tomassian suggests skipping the cleanse if your skin feels dry when you wake up. Follow with a good antioxidant like an L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) serum or one with tetrahexyldecyl ascorbate (THD), silymarin, or phloretin. Layer on a PDRN moisturizer and SPF before any makeup.

Sources indicate that night: Before bed, cleanse thoroughly to remove makeup and sunscreen. Layer on a copper peptide serum, ptiox treatment, tretinoin (retinol), and a PDRN moisturizer. Obagi also suggests combining a pigment-correcting serum with a retinoid to help build the dermis extracellular matrix and target hyperpigmentation.

Industry observers note that bonus steps: Exfoliate one to two times each week with a combination peel pad, alpha hydroxy or beta hydroxy acids depending on your skin’s dryness level or if you’re experiencing any breakout. Tomassian warns, though, that post-40 skin should avoid over-exfoliating. “Skin gets drier with age, and breaking down your skin barrier by scrubbing or peeling too aggressively or too often can leave skin vulnerable to drying out,” he explains.

Industry observers note that at any age, consistency is key. Even if you’re lucky enough to have minimal signs of aging, both experts agree that these steps will go a long way. “It is still notable to incorporate a retinoid, an antioxidant, and a good moisturizer into your daily routine,” says Obagi.

Recent findings suggest that there’s plenty you can do at home to care for your skin after 40, including adding LED light therapy to your lineup to help with fine lines and wrinkles and stimulate collagen—but Tomassian notes these are only beneficial if you use them consistently. An even greater investment is pairing your home routine with regular visits to a professional for in-office procedures like microneedling or ablative and nonablative lasers. These treatments can jump-start your skin to start producing more collagen. For chronic sun damage like redness and dark spots, Tomassian recommends Intense Pulsed Light (IPL), Picosure, or DermaV/Fraxel/CO2 lasers. These devices target pigmentation concerns that skin care does little to improve.

Obagi adds that pro visits are crucial since collagen production peaks at age 18 and, with each passing year, our skin makes 1 percent less collagen, elastin, and GAGs. “By our mid-30s and early 40s, we would benefit from devices that boost collagen production periodically. These can be noninvasive lasers, microneedling, and radiofrequency devices. These will boost collagen for a short time, but when combined with a well-thought-out skin care regimen, the results can be prolonged,” states Obagi.

Sources indicate that you’ve lived with your skin for 40+ years, so you can tell when things start to change. Obagi claims you have to listen to your own skin. “If you are on the dry side or have fragile skin, avoid harsh ingredients such as glycolic or lactic acid, strong retinoids, or over-exfoliating with scrubs. These can irritate the skin and drive sensitivity,” she highlights. If you have thicker skin or are oilier, she suggests exfoliating fruit acids and says your skin can tolerate stronger retinoids.

Tomassian’s rule of thumb is that after age 30, use as many ingredients as possible to bank collagen and focus on thicker moisturizers as you get older, since we produce less oil.

Key ingredients: oat-derived surfactants, plant-derived humectants, polyhydroxy acids.

Key ingredients: liposomal tranexamic acid (TXA), oligopeptide-68, THD, and hydrolyzed algin to help target the various pathways driving pigmentation.

Key ingredients: stabilized vitamin C, hyaluronic acid, panthenol, soothing allantoin, and green tea extract.

Key ingredients: collagen, copper peptides, smoothing and brightening niacinamide, retinal, rice PDRN.

Key ingredients: low-molecular PDRN, moisturizing squalane, panthenol, and ceramide, brightening niacinamide, firming rose peptide.

Key ingredients: glycolic acid, lactic acid, malic acid, antioxidant-rich resveratrol, and green tea extract.

Key ingredients: 10 percent Homosalate, 5 percent Octisalate, 3 percent Avobenzone, brightening niacinamide and ethyl ascorbic acid; moisturizing argan oil, squalane, and bisabolol.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it’s been an incredible year in New York City.
  • According to recent reports, in the latest Saturday Night Live, the sketch of the night was easily “Central Park Horse & Carriage Ride.” Mulaney plays an off-kilter horse-cab driver (“You just trust me implicitly?
  • It has been revealed that the sketch is unofficially a tribute to Broadway—a Latest York cultural staple—with short songs that pay homage to shows like Little Shop of Horrors, Funny Girl, Annie Get Your Gun, and West Side Story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’s been an incredible year in New York City. The start of Zohran Mamdani’s mayoralship set a joyful tone that underscored the city’s immaculate vibe these last few months: the Knicks’ championship win, Harry Styles’ MSG residency, and a Saturday Halloween/Sunday marathon double whammy. So leave it to John Mulaney to take the city down a peg.

According to recent reports, in the latest Saturday Night Live, the sketch of the night was easily “Central Park Horse & Carriage Ride.” Mulaney plays an off-kilter horse-cab driver (“You just trust me implicitly? You realize I have a top hat and a whip, right?”) who highlights two tourists, played by Kam Patterson and Marcello Hernández, the best and worst of New York. With the impending ban on horse-drawn carriages in Central Park slated for June 2028, this is among the last times anyone can tour the city like this.

It has been revealed that the sketch is unofficially a tribute to Broadway—a Latest York cultural staple—with short songs that pay homage to shows like Little Shop of Horrors, Funny Girl, Annie Get Your Gun, and West Side Story. The buzzy Oh, Mary! gets a major tip of the hat too, with current star Bowen Yang making a surprise return to 30 Rockefeller Plaza.

After a mandatory number pointing out that Central Park isn’t safe at night, you get Kenan Thompson as a weed cloud, Tommy Brennan as a rival pedicab cyclist (“I’ll take you to the MoMA/Put you in a coma” is a bar, I’m sorry), and a genuine crowd-pleasing duet with James Austin Johnson and Jeremy Culhane who sing “about a boy named Mamdani.” And there’s Yang, as “Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel,” who sings a cover of “And I Am Telling You” about commuting through Latest Jersey.

But really, the biggest showstopper of the sketch and frankly all of Saturday Night Live this week is VERONIKA SLOWIKOWSKA. As a marathon runner who still hasn’t finished the race, Slowikowska shows off her golden pipes in a cover/parody of “Don’t Rain on My Parade.” Plainly, she crushes it. It’s moments like these that make you remember that SNL is full of overqualified, overly energetic theater kids now, and not stand-up comics blitzed out on cocaine.

You can watch the sketch in the embed below.

The sketch was maybe the best part of a pretty standout SNL, which was owed to the simple fact that Mulaney was the host. A former show writer turned seven-time guest host, Mulaney’s presence was essentially permission to let everyone’s hair down so they could take bigger swings. Mulaney himself stated it: “I used to be a writer at this show, and one of the only difficult things about working here was dealing with the host. So it’s fun when I host, because it’s like there’s no host.” Kinda explains the sketch.
