📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, florence Pugh is making sure every person who helped make her career possible gets their due. In her Women in Hollywood speech, the Dune: Part Three star reflected on what a “bonkers ride” it is to be a woman in the industry. “Being bold and powerful and opinionated—always opinionated—and then vulnerable whenever the cameras need, is a skill I’m still in awe of all of us being able to do,” she stated. “Thank you, ELLE, for honoring all of these powerhouse women.”.

She went on to acknowledge the “thousands of people” who helped make her career possible. Being an actress was a childhood dream. “When I was child, I was asked what I wanted to be when I grew up, and it was this,” she recalled. “But I didn’t know what ‘this’ was, though. I just saw the women and men on my TV and would feel supremely jittery and thrilled watching them. I would get close to the screen, so close I could feel the warmth and static and study all of their faces. I would mainly get jealous of men actually, and weirdly, he’s in my speech, Matt Damon, I was just always jealous of him. And I don’t know why! I don’t! He’s got it all!

In a recent development, “I knew I wanted to do that,” she continued. “All of it, the bells, the whistles. The ability to be free and perform and live in make-believe. The thing is, I wasn’t aware that the biggest and best thing about working in this industry was yet to come. Yes, the explosions and close-ups and locations and free breakfast, lunch, and dinner is cool, but when I truly sit and think about how I got here, it’s down to the thousands of people who have been a part of my career all the way through. They made the path smooth so I could climb to the top of the mountain and wave my flag, which is what I am doing right now. My career and existence in this job is down to thousands of people.

Recent findings suggest that “I think of the crews I’ve been lucky enough to work with, who create the space and the stage so I can do what I do comfortably. I think of the casting directors at the beginning of my career, who took a risk arguing for me, claiming that it didn’t matter that I had no qualifications and only one film credit. Or for the dressers, who would fib and say there was a costume malfunction when they could see I hadn’t had enough time to eat my lunch—this was pre-SAG membership. So don’t panic, SAG. Or to the glam teams all over the world who join because they believe in you and what you do. The makeup artists and hair stylists who wash and clean brushes well into the night just for you, tomorrow at 5 A.M.”.

“I think of all of these people who protected me on my journey,” she said. “And it would not have been possible without every single one of them. Just in case you’re listening now and you’re not aware how grateful we are and how important you are, I just received an ELLE Women of the Year honor, and I didn’t get here on my own. I only took stock in myself because I could see you doing it for me first.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson has officially received his license to kill. As James Bond, that is. Hollywood’s favorite leading man was announced as the next 007 on Monday, November 16, after Puck News reported that he screen-tested for the role in the eleventh hour.

In a recent development, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Robert wrote in a statement, per ABC News. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

It has been revealed that as it turns out, Robert has unknowingly manifested the role of a lifetime throughout his banger-after-banger career. No, seriously—R-Patz locked into Ariana Grande as Galinda-levels of manifesting here, whether he believes it or not.

In a recent development, even after all these years as a Twihard, I’m genuinely shocked at how much this man was asked about potentially playing the famous spy. So, for the sake of your scrolling time, I’ve rounded up all the times Robert Pattinson manifested his role as James Bond, right here.

Industry observers note that all roads lead back to Twilight. Robert got his major break playing swoonworthy sparkly vampire Edward Cullen in the film franchise, and the first movie lowkey predicted his current role as 007. Don’t believe me? Check out this scene.

When Bella’s friend group discusses the school’s upcoming Monte Carlo prom theme, Eric says, “Gambling, tuxedos, and Bond, James Bond,” before the camera cuts to Edward and Bella stepping out of his car.

Recent findings suggest that robert starred alongside another Bond, Pierce Brosnan, in 2010’s Remember Me. While doing press for the movie, he was constantly asked whether he’d want to take on the iconic role at some point.

During an interview with Fandango, he admitted that he would “quite like to play a villain in a Bond film.”.

“That would be fun,” he continued. “Or maybe a male, like, Bond girl. A Bond boy.”.

The BBC separately asked if he’d be into the role, to which he sheepishly responded, “Oh, I don’t know. That’s quite significant shoes to fill. If I did it right now, it’d probably be pretty bad. Pretty embarrassing.”.

He remained humble at the time, but fast forward 16 years, and he’s officially been cast as 007 himself!

The Bond questions kept coming after Remember Me, though Daniel Craig had led the franchise since 2005.

During an interview with Shortlist, Rob noted he was open to taking on the role in the future.

In a recent development, “Yeah definitely, but more like 20 years,” he said. “I think there’d be nothing worse than, like, ‘Let’s get a fresh-faced Bond!’ That would be the worst idea in the world. After Daniel Craig, you have to have some baggage. It would be ridiculous to reinvent [him] as some young posh kid. Or, if [he] was, I’d have to get so tortured in the first few scenes. I’d have to do the first film with one arm or something.”.

Recent findings suggest that in a separate conversation with the BBC, Rob was asked about the role again, responding, “Why do you keep asking me this? There already is a James Bond. I don’t know. I mean, I love James Bond. So, I don’t know.”.

Okay, so this technically wasn’t spoken prophecy from R-Patz, but someone previously tied to another Bond project expressed interest in seeing the actor take on the famous role.

Danny Boyle, who was originally tapped to direct the last Bond movie, No Time to Die, told The Guardian that while he watched Robert’s flick High Life, “I was sitting there thinking: ‘Oh my God, they should get him to be the next Bond.’”.

#31298. Timothy Dalton's 007 Advice Is the Only Guidance Robert Pattinson Should Follow

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1965 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Timothy Dalton's 007 Advice Is the Only Guidance Robert Pattinson Should Follow

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that james Bond’s greatest weakness is not megalomaniacal madmen bent on world domination.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s why Robert Pattinson’s casting as filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming 007 is a bold and promising choice.
  • According to recent reports, some things shouldn’t change, like his seductiveness, the Walther PPK, and the way he likes his martinis to be shaken.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that james Bond’s greatest weakness is not megalomaniacal madmen bent on world domination. Those he can handle. The superspy is far more likely to be taken down by well-meaning committees.

Recent findings suggest that that’s why Robert Pattinson’s casting as filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming 007 is a bold and promising choice. The two of them together have amassed enough industry clout to craft the character their own way, to make him distinctive and daring in a way, hopefully, that we haven’t seen before.

According to recent reports, some things shouldn’t change, like his seductiveness, the Walther PPK, and the way he likes his martinis to be shaken. But those things only make up the silhouette of James Bond. Each actor must put his own imprint on the core of Ian Fleming’s debonair secret agent, just as the author did in his original novels. Sean Connery added ruggedness to the savoir faire. George Lazenby gave him a soulful vulnerability in his solo outing as the character. Roger Moore sharpened 007’s sense of humor. Each actor leaves his fingerprints behind as he hands it off to the next.

This leads to the essential question for anyone signing up to play James Bond: Are you strong enough to stand out?

It’s not so easily answered. I’ll let Timothy Dalton, my personal favorite Bond, explain: “I have some good friends from the Bond days, some really good people, but they’re trapped. Everyone’s trapped by it in a way,” he told me. “Whoever does it has got to have a very clear sense of what they want to achieve, because everybody in the world has got a different opinion about it.”.

To figure out what comes next, we should look back at what came before.

Dalton (who happens to be Christopher Nolan’s favorite Bond too) made that comment to me back in February 2025, when Amazon MGM Studios first acquired the rights to the 007 character.

When he first took on the role in 1987’s The Living Daylights, his choice was to add a renegade wolf quality. But he also recognized that James Bond must remain, ultimately, the good guy, and that movie was entirely defined by an act of mercy. Fleming’s short story “The Living Daylights” makes up the film’s opening scene: Bond has been sent to take out an enemy sniper, but when he sees that his target is a beautiful cellist (played by Maryam d’Abo), he aims his own rifle to distract her rather than kill her.

He then becomes responsible for her life, and his 007 has no problem cutting down any foes who block their paths. Dalton’s Bond was more polished than Connery and less comedic than Moore, but he was led by a kind of stormy passion. He had heart, but it pumped cold blood.

In a recent development, still, Dalton had to break through that formidable wall of consensus. Bond is not a solo enterprise, of course. The director has a say, as do the producers and the screenwriters, but the danger comes from two places: the studio and the audience itself. As Dalton said, “Everybody in the world has got a different opinion about it,” and those voices have to be defied, just as his 007 refused the order to place a bullet in the enemy cellist’s heart.

Nothing makes hands wring and sweat pour in a studio conference room like something unexpected, and know-it-all supposed “fans” often resist change while paradoxically demanding something fresh and new. He had two outings as Bond, the second being 1989’s License to Kill, in which 007 goes even more rogue, defying Her Majesty’s secret service to embark on a mission of revenge. Then the character became tied up in rights lawsuits for several years, and Dalton chose not to return.

Recent findings suggest that when Daniel Craig took over 007 from Pierce Brosnan in 2005, purists complained about his blue eyes and blond hair. When they finally saw him bring the character to life in 2006’s Casino Royale, those critics soon fell silent. Craig gave Bond a soldier’s mindset. He was a battlefield veteran whose new uniform happens to be a dashing suit. He was successful for so long because as he added his own spin, he capitalized on the best of what came before: He was as rough as Connery and as lethal as Dalton. The humor and playfulness that defined Moore and Brosnan were still present, but they served as a mask for the kind of wounded vulnerability that Lazenby had introduced.

Pattinson is now free to pick and choose whatever qualities he likes from this Brotherhood of Bond, but if he is going to take anyone’s advice, it should be Dalton’s: “Whoever does it has got to have a very clear sense of what they want to achieve.”.

According to recent reports, fortunately, no one tells Villeneuve what to do. The filmmaker has spent two decades establishing himself not just as a distinctive artist but as a reliable box-office draw. Those two qualities give him a powerful weapon—clout—that can stave off the onslaught of opinions that will inevitably surround this casting choice.

Just this Saturday, I moderated a Q&A with Villeneuve at the Golden Globe Foundation before an audience of students, and one young filmmaker named Oscar Flores asked the Dune filmmaker, “When is the right time for you to listen to feedback, and when is the right time to listen to yourself?”.

It has been revealed that villeneuve gave an answer that perfectly matches Dalton’s advice and increases my optimism about his approach to Bond: “Honestly, people say that I’m humble, but that’s bullshit,” he remarked, only partly joking. “If I’m asking for $200 million for a movie, what kind of humility is that?”.

The suggestion he made to the students was to not take on projects that are outside their control. Start small, stay true, and build up your skill set behind the camera while establishing a reputation that gives you defining power over the movies you make. He warned them not to follow the “siren” song of a significant-budget offer if it means ceding control. Instead, Villeneuve said, he found it effective to build up his status with smaller films, moving from 2010’s more intimate Incendies to 2013’s harrowing Prisoners and 2015’s even more sprawling Sicario before leveling up in scale to 2016’s Arrival and 2017’s Blade Runner 2049.

“The thing that I did when I was a young filmmaker is that I tried not to jump steps,” he told us at the Golden Globes Foundation forum. “I went step-by-step on projects. I was able to keep control of them. I was making sure that I was in control of the tools, and control of the language, and getting strong with the crew, being able to and making sure that my voice would be heard. … What I will say to you is: Be careful of the sirens.”.

Only after amassing this authority, Villeneuve said, did he feel the time was right to take on his dream project of Dune. “If you made a successful first feature film that cost $200,000 and they offer you a major blockbuster, be careful,” he said this weekend. “Be careful who you are working with, and don’t listen to your ego. Do you really believe that you have the skills to bring it to the screen? Maybe you do. Some people can, by the way. I was not ready to make Dune after my second [film]. ... It took me a lot of movies before I knew that I was able to handle the pressure and making sure that I would be able to control totally, 100 percent, the film. At the end of the day when I look at the movie and the screen, it’s my movie.”.

No doubt Pattinson’s casting was his decision, and Villeneuve’s status ensured it was accepted by the powers that be at Amazon MGM Studios. It probably wasn’t a difficult yes, given that Pattinson is right now in his prime. Not only is he The Batman, but he stood out as the conniving usurper Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and has earned accolades for his haunting performance as a predator-hunting journalist in Primetime.

Is he a heartthrob? Ask the legion of Twilight fans, and cover your ears for their deafening reply.

Recent findings suggest that pattinson forged his bond with Villeneuve with another upcoming role in Dune: Part Three, playing the Face Dancer Scytale. He’s a shape-shifting psychological assassin who seeks to undermine Timothée Chalamet’s all-seeing, all-powerful emperor by getting inside his head, and the actor and filmmaker worked closely to figure out the look, mannerisms, and motivations of a creature void of form.

As Pattinson said in a recent cover story I wrote for Empire magazine about Dune: Part Three: “I went into it being like, ‘I want to look like an alien,’ and initially Denis was saying, ‘Well, I think he’s got to fit in with everybody. I think he just looks like you. He’s normal,’ ” Pattinson said. The actor was candid about his own reaction: “I was a little bit disappointed.”.

According to recent reports, then Villeneuve thought about it some more. As the director told those students on Saturday, he has a strong point of view, but it’s not inflexible. Villeneuve is not interested in the whims of a crowd, but he is very open to suggestions from creative partners. If their own insights open his eyes to a possibility he hadn’t considered, he will seize upon the ideas.

Sources indicate that shortly before shooting, Villeneuve reversed course on Scytale, and Pattinson noted the filmmaker sent him an email with a newly introduced look for the Face Dancer. Pale skin, white hair, no eyebrows, which has the effect of making his expressions somewhat inscrutable. In other words, a blank page, upon which the characteristics of others can be written as he shifts his own natural shape. Pattinson said he felt relief: “I’m like, ‘Okay, this is very much not like a normal guy at all.’ ”.

This anecdote is meaningful for 007 because it reveals that the filmmaker and the star can share ideas, experiment and explore, and listen to each other. That’s the collaboration this character needs.

Industry observers note that at 40, Pattinson is not the youngest possible Bond, but he brings life experience that will be vital for playing a character who needs a certain prowess and wisdom to survive. He and Villeneuve both have a kind of double-0 swagger that will allow them to ignore the cacophonous advice of the masses and devise something original.

Pattinson has been doing this for a long time. Consider his doomed Cedric Diggory in 2005’s Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, another character—like Bond, Bruce Wayne, and Edward Cullen—who exists as an intense, preexisting image in the minds of millions of fans. But with his brooding presence, he added uncertainty to Cedric’s innate decency and fair-mindedness. The kid who dramatically hops down from a tree in his jump-scare introduction to Ron and Harry could very well have been there to bully them. That’s a sneak-attack entrance, proposed by Pattinson himself, and little details like that gave this upright, wholesome character a dose of intrigue.

Sources indicate that pattinson was only 17 when he filmed that. In the more than two decades that followed, he has paid his dues, learned his lessons, and no doubt gotten his share of scars. With Villeneuve backing him, he’s bulletproof. The two of them can take chances, be bold, and defy orders—just like 007 would, just as playing the character demands.

Pattinson is not a paper doll that will fold when the committees come for James Bond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, it’s been a significant year for shoes. In addition to the supreme reign of the It shoe, designers have fully entered a new era of experimentalism when it comes to footwear. And truly, nothing feels off-limits. Earlier this year, Schiaparelli took the cake with faux-taxidermy kitten heels, replete with shockingly lifelike snarling cat heads, eyes, whiskers, and tongues included. As did Prada, with Victorian-style boots covered in a collage of feathers and decadent, chandelier-studded low heels straight out of a Marie Antoinette fever dream. Fashion insiders and the masses got swept up in the hunt for Chanel’s ponyhair ballet flats, in a moment that felt like a new level of footwear obsession. Now, we have the runway-approved gardening shoe. Dior, TWP, and Public School have all shown their own takes on the look, each reinterpreting a classic garden clog.

Consider it the fashion equivalent of touching grass in the digital age. Gardening shoes have a clear connection to nature that is quite literally (and aesthetically) grounding. With their neutral beige tones and down-to-earth materials, they read as the opposite of the feathers, crystals, and animal-themed ponyhair of It shoes of the last few seasons. The garden-ready shoe combines the unapologetic high-fashion ugly-chic notion with the idea of practicality.

Sources indicate that at Miu Miu fall/winter 2026, the runway was literally a mossy, grassy display ripe for stomping around in lug soles, and that’s what the models did, in bubble-soled slip-ons and chunky lace-up boots that almost looked like something you’d go hiking in, paired with technical nylon jackets and funky fedoras. Miu Miu called it “Clothes that are a method of self-preservation, a means of valuing that inside,” in the show notes. “They emblematize the individual, and in turn the identity of Miu Miu itself.”.

There’s also undoubtedly a little bit of irony to this style. Most of the gardening shoes on the runway serve as a high-contrast answer to flashy, anything-but-toned-down runway garments. Take Loewe’s slip-on shoes with a rubberized toe that also looked ready for the task of planting biennials and perennials. They were styled with lush shearlings and near-neon orange latex dresses, the shoes put the classic jolie laide terminology to work. Shoes, after all, have for decades served as storytelling anchors within fashion collections. Elsewhere at Dior’s spring/summer 2027 show in Paris, brown suede shoes were capped off with rubberized toes and practical soles, worn with silk petal jackets and textural, couture-like miniskirts.

In a recent development, simone Rocha just released its final collaboration with Crocs, including a Quick Trail Racer style that looks like something a real gardener would wear, only with Simone Rocha’s saccharine crystals and ruffles. Retailers have seen the look come and go: “The garden-like lug sole trend ebbs and flows in the background of footwear,” Moda Operandi’s Ryan Kleman, VP of buying, accessories, tells ELLE. “Ultimately, the appeal mostly stems from the idea of putting outfits together ‘with the wrong shoe.’ The garden shoe is the wrong shoe, in many ways. Otherwise, the shoe’s practicality and function underscore how easily customers can convert to them.”.

The It shoe is officially grounded.

Here’s what to expect during tonight’s episode, and how many couples will be going home.

Most likely, the show will eliminate just one couple during tonight’s semifinals—which means five couples will be in the finals next week.

However, it’s possible that the judges will decide to keep everyone. Host Alfonso Ribeiro was asked about the possibility of six couples being in the finale back in September and had this to say:.

Just FYI, everyone was safe during the season 32 and season 33 semifinals, but the season 31 semifinals included a double elimination. In other words, anything could happen!

In a recent development, all signs point to yes! That said, there have been reports that Maura had to postpone/cancel several rehearsals due to injury.

“She reinjured the rib over the weekend and had to postpone another rehearsal and get looked at by medics again,” a source told The Sun. “She’s trying to give it her all but giving it her all is costing her physically. The six remaining couples will perform two dances each tonight: a Latin dance and a ballroom dance.

Connor and Arnold: a Jive to “Blue Suede Shoes” by Elvis Presley and a Quickstep to “Dance Dance” by Fall Out Boy.

Amber and Pasha: a Salsa to “Bemba Colorá” by Celia Cruz and a Viennese waltz to “Dangerous Woman” by Ariana Grande.

Tatyana and Jan: a Cha-cha to “I Like It Like That” by Pete Rodríguez and a Waltz to “Open Arms” by Journey.

It has been revealed that harry and Jenna: a Paso doble to “We Found Love” by Rihanna feat. Calvin Harris and a Quickstep to “Valerie” by Mark Ronson ft. Amy Winehouse.

Ezra and Daniella: a Jive to “Footloose” by Kenny Loggins and a Quickstep to “Kryptonite” by 3 Doors Down.

Maura and Mark: a Samba to “Samba Vocalizado” by Luciano Perrone and a Viennese waltz to “Shrike” by Hozier.

Dancing With the Stars airs its semifinals on Tuesday, November 17, at 8 p.m. ET on Disney+ and ABC.

Recent findings suggest that it’s been a tough few days for Duffy, and Duffy has been huffy. From Friday’s press conference with Markwayne Mullin, to his own microphonically challenged solo outing on Saturday, through all five morning-show appearances, Duffy has checked all the boxes the modern Republican official must: look aggrieved, place blame elsewhere, praise the president, be white. It’s all television, after all, and there’s a role to be played.

According to recent reports, sean Duffy has been at this for decades. You know he was on the sixth season of The Real World, and you know he met his wife and fellow Real Worlder Rachel Campos when they participated in an early season of what would become The Real World/Road Rules Challenge. But when you really go back and look, you’ll see that they’ve both been practicing for this moment since the ’90s. Game recognizes game; as a fellow alumnus of 20th-century MTV, let me walk you through it.

It has been revealed that the Real World was born when MTV decided to try its hand at creating a weekly soap opera, in the style of the era-defining Beverly Hills 90210 and Melrose Place. But cable budgets being what they are, a full scripted show was untenable, so producers had the bold idea to do away with actors and writers entirely. The first couple seasons of The Real World kept the focus on art by casting young artists: Julie the emerging dancer amid the model and writer and singer-songwriters in season 1, Jon the wannabe Garth Brooks in season 2. But that went out the window quick, as producers and aspiring castmates figured out the same thing at the same time: The job was to stir the pot. So by season 3, deeply unpleasant bike messenger Puck was dropped into the San Francisco house to clash with saintly AIDS educator Pedro, with whom conservative Rachel initially refused to share a bathroom for fear of sink-based HIV transmission. In 1994.

By season 6, casts seemed chosen specifically to play a predetermined part and drive each other up the wall. Real World: Boston features Stanford med student Kameelah and ladies man Syrus, Catholic Texan Elka and Manhattan-born mess on wheels Montana. And then there was Sean Duffy, Wisconsin boy, lumberjack-games participant, and future secretary of transportation. Sean occupied the Cute Boy spot in the cast that had been held by Aaron in Los Angeles and St. Louis race car driver Mike in London. But this being 1997, he was also a different cultural archetype: the knee-jerk Rush Limbaugh–era conservative. Accent on jerk. Here’s a moment when Sean makes fun of Elka’s underwear and then immediately denies it.

It has been revealed that just straight-up, reflexively, smoothly denying he did something we just saw him do, because he did it on camera and into a microphone. Lying with a straight face. This would become a job skill.

It’s a little like something we saw Sean’s future wife Rachel do on her season. In an early episode, she engages in the hot, safe rebellious act of 1994 by getting her navel pierced. In a later episode, she gets a telephone call from her angry mother, who has seen the belly-button bauble in a photograph (a physical photograph, sent through the U.S. Mail—again, we lived differently in the ’90s). Rachel assures her mother it’s not a piercing but instead a sticker she put there. Forget the fact that, again, all of this is on camera and the mom is going to learn the truth soon enough. Watching back then, I remember thinking two things: One, this person lies very easily, and two, I think she might be one of those people who’s conservative just so they don’t upset their parents.

Anyway. Sean and Rachel did The Challenge and got married and had three hundred and fifty children. Sean became a congressman for Wisconsin; Rachel tried out for The View but never quite nailed it and now she’s on Fox & Friends sometimes. And because it all comes back to reality television and personal branding, the Duffy family spent a few weeks of Sean’s tenure as secretary of transportation to film a show. The Great American Road Trip was supposed to have aired on Fox Nation, but instead it got dumped onto YouTube, where most episodes are hovering around 10k views.

Also, Duffy’s son-in-law Michael Alfonso, who’s 26, is set to become the youngest person in Congress, having won a seat in Wisconsin’s 7th District in this month’s elections. Alfonso’s campaign was buoyed by generous campaign donations from numerous transportation companies, executives, and lobbyists, including a $2,500 contribution from Air Space Intelligence’s PAC in March. In June, the FAA awarded the AI start-up a contract worth up to $875.95 million. The tech giant’s SMART system went nationwide days before the November 13 ground stop, though the FAA and the company said the outage was unrelated to SMART.

According to recent reports, I’m sure it’s nothing. But I’m even more sure Duffy will say it is.

The way that John F. Kennedy understood television in the way Richard Nixon did not, Sean Duffy understands reality television in a way few others do. He’s lived it. He understands it as a marketing exercise. Knowing your brand, hitting the beats of the scene you’re supposed to play, showing up with a yearbook picture-day haircut and lying with a smile will get you far in this world. Whether he survives this turbulence or not, he’s learned that lesson.

According to recent reports, sean and Rachel have been at this for decades, but as viewers so have we. We can see them as they are: dishonest children, playing a role, begging for approval, just trying not to get yelled at.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that we love fisherman sweaters for the same reason we love a great martini: They’re classic, and they’re comforting.
  • Industry observers note that now, it’s crucial to remember that when it comes to the backstory of most garments, there tends to be a lot of lore mixed in with the genuine history.
  • It has been revealed that in 2026, you probably don’t need a fisherman sweater to keep you warm while you’re on the water off Ireland’s west coast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we love fisherman sweaters for the same reason we love a great martini: They’re classic, and they’re comforting. A proper fisherman knit brings the whole winter wardrobe into alignment. The chunky texture instantly upgrades jeans and boots, warmth doesn’t sacrifice style, and that easy, rugged-prep vibe that works at the office as well as it does on the couch. In other words, it’s the rare cold-weather staple that’s as practical as it is handsome.

Industry observers note that now, it’s crucial to remember that when it comes to the backstory of most garments, there tends to be a lot of lore mixed in with the genuine history. That said, here’s how the story generally goes. Traditional fisherman sweaters hail from Ireland, where in the late 1800s to the mid-1900s, they were popular for men who had to work long hours on fishing boats. Usually, fisherman sweaters were hand-knit by their wives or by local artisans, and they were always designed to be sturdy and warm, keeping the wind and chill out. Cable-knit patterns became popular for fisherman sweaters. You might know these sweaters as Aran sweaters, referencing the Aran Islands, where the textured design has become a specialty.

It has been revealed that in 2026, you probably don’t need a fisherman sweater to keep you warm while you’re on the water off Ireland’s west coast. (Or maybe you do! We don’t know your story.) However, you do need a fisherman sweater for the sheer coziness and looks they provide, though. Our favorite options of all time are below, tested and reviewed by Esquire editors (with some photographed on Esquire’s editor in chief, Michael Sebastian). Anyway, these fisherman sweaters are seriously making us want to take some fishing lessons. Anyone know where we can do that?

Industry observers note that you don’t need to break the bank for a high-quality fisherman sweater that’ll last you years to come. Quince is proof. Crafted from organic cotton, this thick, warm sweater is a perfect layering piece for winter—put a tee or a button-down underneath, a topcoat or a puffer on top, and you’re golden. The rib detailing offers some extra texture and style, and relaxed raglan sleeves offer more freedom of movement.

Ok, so the pictured sweater is no longer in stock. The cable knit rollneck was seasonal, but there is always a fisherman-y option in the collection. Honestly, whichever J. Crew rollneck hits this bar at any point in time, that’s likely my favorite fisherman sweater of the moment.

L.L. Bean crafts a classic fisherman sweater to a tee. It has everything you’d want in the style: a thick, heavyweight fabric that carries some structure with it; a cable-knit design; and thick cotton yarn that keeps the chill out and the warmth in. This style is a go-to for something timeless without too much fuss or frill. It has a slim fit, so if you want something baggier, more classically cut, make sure to size up.

Okay, hear me out—this isn’t your traditional fisherman sweater, but you can make a damn good excuse for Polo Ralph Lauren’s ultra-soft, ultra-luxe cable-knit sweater when you feel how unbelievably plush this is. This is the fisherman sweater you go to when you want something distinctly elevated and chic but you still want to have a cable-knit design and a fit you can dress down with joggers and slides.

Recent findings suggest that you may already know that we at Esquire have an affinity for shawl collar cardigans. With their laid-back Western vibes and classic Americana silhouette, shawl collar cardigans look handsome on just about any guy. One of our favorites is this fisherman style from Filson. It’s made from thick, warm cotton and features a classic button front and ribbing on the hem and cuffs.

If you, like commerce editor Luke Guillory, aren’t into the super chunky fisherman sweaters and are looking for something a little more lightweight that you can easily layer, this Buck Mason pick should be right up your alley. Luke has even endorsed the style, lauding the sweater for its warm yet lightweight feel, perfect not-too-boxy but not-too-slim cut, and durable cotton that can be machine washed and still not miss a beat.

Recent findings suggest that this gorgeous wool fisherman sweater is from Finisterre, a surf clothing brand from Cornwall, England, so it’s specifically made for cold, windy days on the water. It’s made from 100 percent heavyweight, pure new wool with a natural crimp, which means it creates natural pockets of air to help insulate you (even if you’re not on the water). One writer says it’s one of his go-to winter sweaters.

Industry observers note that brooks Brothers’ woolly sweater is so damn good I might just have to take up the art of fishing to pay proper tribute to it. With a soft and cozy yet breathable wool fabric and cable-knit pattern, this relaxed style puts a contemporary spin on the traditional fisherman sweater. It’s warm, soft, and stylish, and it looks just as good with dress pants and loafers as it does with jeans and sneakers.

Begg x Co’s Isla cashmere sweater is another fantastic, high-quality cashmere option. It’s just oppressively beautiful. Begg x Co operates its own mills in Scotland, which reveals up in the world-class materials and construction, but the vibe isn’t overly capital-F-Fashion the way some French or Italian luxury brands can feel. It’s timeless, understated luxury. Made from 8‑ply cashmere, it lands in a perfect mid-weight sweet spot for fall and winter: substantial and warm without being bulky. It’s definitely quite pricey, but you’re paying for the highest level of quality and finish.

This sweater from Ghiaia Cashmere is divine, surprising considering the brand is based out of southern California. The mock neck is the star here—cozy without the bulk of a turtleneck—and the rich brown color is lovely (though it also comes in a clean cream if you want something lighter). A chest pocket adds a surprisingly practical touch, making it feel more functional than you’d ever expect a sweater to be.

It has been revealed that the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County has brought a bunch of fresh faces to the franchise, including podcaster Bobbi Althoff. Of course, that includes her personal life and her relationship with basketball player Tyler “Ty” Hawkins.

While we saw him accompany Bobbi to several events throughout the spin-off’s inaugural season, the pair is unfortunately no longer together after filming. After months of breakup speculation, Ty revealed he and Bobbi quietly split in September due to “different” lifestyles.

After posting the breakup announcement, Ty spoke with People about the split—and admitted it’s been “tough” watching SLOMW: OC knowing they’re no longer a couple.

It has been revealed that “Actually seeing us as a couple knowing that we aren’t together was tough. I miss her and everything and the life that we had,” he told the outlet, emphasizing that they ended things amicably.

In a recent development, “She’s been getting great feedback, which is all I can hope for,” he said of his ex’s involvement on the Hulu reality series. “It’s great to see her flourish.”.

Bobbi and Tyler dated for nearly two years, marking her first public relationship after her split from ex-husband Cory Althoff in 2024.

She has yet to comment on Tyler’s breakup comments.

I Have Serious Questions About the 2026 Grammy Nominations

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Grammys, more than any other awards-voting body of the big EGOT four, is easily the most chaotic.
  • The Recording Academy confirmed on Monday, November 16, that Kanye West is a Grammy nominee once again.
  • So, before the Grammys decide to ignore all of our desires and complaints and just shower Taylor Swift with more little golden phonographs on February 7, 2027, let’s try to make sense of the 2026 Grammy nominees below.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grammys, more than any other awards-voting body of the big EGOT four, is easily the most chaotic. Sure, we can shake our fists in the air all day about how Stanley Kubrick somehow never won an Oscar, or ask ourselves why the Tony Awards ever allowed themselves to become a place where SpongeBob SquarePants: The Broadway Musical leads with 12 nominees. But recalling Grammy events like Macklemore beating Kendrick Lamar, Esperanza Spalding claiming Best New Artist over Justin Bieber and Drake, and Beck taking home Album of the Year instead of Beyoncé, it’s a wonder just what happens between when the votes are submitted and when the winners are revealed.

This year? The Recording Academy confirmed on Monday, November 16, that Kanye West is a Grammy nominee once again. And there’s a single category where Bruce Springsteen, Phoebe Bridgers, and Charli XCX are lumped together, so I guess they’re considered basically the same kind of artist to voters. Plus, new ideas like “Best Asian Pop Music Performance” are moving forward despite immediately losing support from the most prominent artist in that category, and Best New Artist nominees can apparently put out their fifth studio album and still be considered. What’s going on?

So, before the Grammys decide to ignore all of our desires and complaints and just shower Taylor Swift with more little golden phonographs on February 7, 2027, let’s try to make sense of the 2026 Grammy nominees below.

Industry observers note that the first thought that entered my mind when I saw this year’s nominees for Album of the Year was, Are we confirming who will be available to perform before announcing the nominees now? Because even if so, I think Bruno Mars would perform either way.

Recent findings suggest that it’s very cool to see how women dominated the music field this year, especially because they truly did. Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers, and Rosalía all earning Album of the Year nominations is a no-brainer. Olivia Dean, who won Best New Artist last year, and Ella Langley, who wrote “Choosin’ Texas,” make up the rest of the list. (Did we really love that entire nineteen-track Langley album?) Plus, of course, the obligatory Taylor Swift nominations.

But were Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas—who are tied with seven nominations each after the leading women, including an Album of the Year nod for Mars—the two men with the best offerings this year?

Sources indicate that bruno Mars had a very good song on The Romantic with “Why You Wanna Fight?” The Luther Vandross-esque R&B ballad was everything you’d look for in a Song of the Year nominee. But instead, it looks like Bruno is going all in on “Risk It All” and “I Just Might,” the latter of which is more of a “Happy” by Pharrell Williams-type song that somehow isn’t the lead single of the next Trolls movie.

Recent findings suggest that sorry Madonna! Apologies Robyn, Tinashe, Slayyter, and every other pop artist who soundtracked our year on the dance floor with some of the best albums of 2026. Breaking into the top four major categories still looks like a no-go.

Sources indicate that instead, Madonna, Robyn, and Tinashe were relegated to categories such as Best Dance Pop Recording and Best Dance/Electronic Album, even despite critical acclaim. If you want a Record of the Year nod, try writing a song for Toy Story 5.

Industry observers note that don Toliver is up for Best New Artist. The Houston rapper, who was signed to Travis Scott’s label in 2018, released his fifth studio album, Octane, this year. He had a song on the F9 soundtrack in 2021—which isn’t even the latest Fast & Furious movie—and his 2023 album, Love Sick, featured James Blake, Future, and Justin Bieber. But here we are, in 2026, watching him compete for Best New Artist.

Sources indicate that equally puzzling: Remi Wolf is nominated for Best Fresh Artist. The singer’s exceptional debut record, Juno, came out in 2021. And her best record to date, Mud, was released recently on October 9, just outside of the Grammy submission window that closed in late August. But following the logic of how Olivia Dean won Best New Artist last year even though Dean’s album is competing this year, it’s clear that the whole Best New Artist category needs some rethinking.

In a recent development, 2026 wasn’t a banner year for rap. I can admit that. Sure, we had very good records from A$AP Rocky, Denzel Curry, Vince Staples, JPEGMAFIA, Isaiah Rashad, Genesis Owusu, and Baby Keem. But none of the musicians I listed above went recognized this year, except for Keem’s single “Best Rap Performance” nomination.

Instead, the Recording Academy nominated Wale’s Everything Is a Lot—the Washington, D.C., rapper’s best and most mature album of the last decade, but far less influential than Rocky’s or Keem’s releases. And if not for Drake’s long-running boycott, the absence of Iceman’s “Janice STFU” just looks silly. But if you want to talk ridiculous, let’s see how Rap Album of the Year nominee Kanye West plays out for the Recording Academy over the next couple of months.

In a recent development, harry Styles won Album of the Year for Harry’s House in 2023. He beat out Un Verano Sin Ti by Bad Bunny, Renaissance by Beyoncé, Mr. Morale & the Substantial Steppers by Kendrick Lamar, and 30 by Adele. It was a major upset. And just last month, the former One Direction member wrapped a historic thirty-night residency at Madison Square Garden in Latest York City in support of his latest album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.

In a recent development, now, I’m not saying Kiss All the Time is a masterwork, but it’s strange that Styles didn’t receive a single nomination for his Harry’s House follow-up. “Aperture” was very catchy! Taylor Swift can’t sneeze without the Recording Academy inventing a newly introduced category for her to compete in. But an artist who just won Album of the Year can find himself completely shut out, even if his latest record is a success?

The global K-pop megastars reunited this year following mandatory military service in South Korea for one of the genre’s most-anticipated albums of all time, ARIRANG. The record paid homage to the popular Korean folk song of the same name while also pushing the K-pop genre forward with hip-hop-heavy material. ARIRANG’s fourteen tracks also filled the top fourteen spots of Spotify’s global Top 50 chart on its first day of release on March 20. I’ll stop there, but there are a hundred more ways to say that it was one of the biggest albums of the year.

But when the Recording Academy confirmed a upcoming category this year, “Best Asian Pop Music Performance,” the group made the decision not to submit for the Grammys this year. The move was widely regarded as a protest of the new category, which many interpreted as a ghettoization to keep the rise of popular Asian acts away from the general field categories. “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group posted on social media.

In a recent development, on Monday, November 16, the Academy went through with the category anyway, announcing nominees including Lisa from Blackpink, the Japanese pop-metal group Babymetal, the K-pop group IVE, and the Filipino girl group Bini, among others. But with BTS joining Drake in his boycott of the Grammys, I wonder how the Recording Academy will fare without two of the world’s most popular acts entertaining its awards show.

In a recent development, the Great Divide, a seventeen-track rock album that turned Kahan into one of the most popular touring musicians of 2026, was considered a favorite to receive a nomination in every major category this year. Songs like “American Cars” dealt with past failures and road trip blues, while lead single “The Great Divide” tackled how fame added extra struggles to many of his already-strained relationships. And Kahan had the resume to become a major category contender this year. He had a Number One record! He did the full press tour, he performed on Saturday Night Live, and he sold out stadiums all across the country.

But it must have been an omen when Kahan sang that “California’s so much more than some awards show” on the deluxe edition’s “Orbiter,” because he received just one nomination on Monday for Best Contemporary Folk Album. It’s a shame.

It has been revealed that best Album Cover is back. The category returned last year and accurately awarded Tyler, the Creator’s zany Chromakopia artwork, which featured the artist wearing a black, ceramic mask. He told Complex at the time that it symbolized how the fresh music was “so honest, that I think I had to wear a mask of my own face to get some of that sh*t out.”.

But what about this year’s nominees? Well, Mavis Staples’s Sad and Beautiful World artwork depicts the artist sitting at a table. Interpol’s This Mirror Weighs a Ton artwork is a chandelier made of security cameras, and Lily Allen’s West End Girl is a painting of the artist wearing a polka-dot jacket. Are these nominees... the best album covers of the year?

Industry observers note that charli XCX’s photograph of Martin Scorsese, John Cale, and Marc Jacobs was easily the much-talked-about album cover of the year, even though Music, Fashion, Film wasn’t nominated. Olivia Rodrigo’s upside-down swinging for you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love is definitely one of the more memorable covers that come to mind. Same goes for Robyn’s blurry and nude Sexistential photo, the politics behind Kneecap’s Fenian, Thundercat biting his dark leather jacket on the cover of Distracted, or even a pregnant Latto posing with a baby tiger for the Big Mama cover ahead of her cheetah-themed baby shower.

We might not have a specific shade of green to color this year and make Best Album Cover an easy choice, but if you’re going to bring the category back? At least wow us.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

P&O Cruises has revealed that it will welcome a line-up of adventurers, broadcasters, sporting icons and storytellers on three of its longer cruises in 2027.

Guests sailing on the Arcadia’s world cruise, the Aurora’s grand tour and the Iona’s 35-night cruise between January and April will hear first-hand stories from remarkable guest speakers.

Carnival UK & P&O Cruises president Paul Ludlow noted: “Our longer holidays give guests the time to explore more of the world and these remarkable speakers will bring another dimension to that sense of discovery.”.

The company said in a press release that the Arcadia guests will hear from Dale Templar, the BAFTA and Emmy-winning wildlife producer and director behind the BBC’s Human Planet.

He will be joined by Rebecca Stephens MBE, the first British woman to climb Mount Everest and complete the Seven Summits and Zelda la Grange, who will share stories from her 19 years working alongside Nelson Mandela.

The line-up also includes Australian rugby icon David Campese; photography industry veteran and Getty Images executive Carmin Romanelli; best-selling author and travel writer Sue Williams and much-loved gardening presenter Charlie Dimmock.

On the Aurora’s grand tour, Royal Marine veteran and adventurer Mitchell Hutchcraft will share the story of his 9,000-mile human-powered journey from England to the summit of Everest.

TV producer, director and expedition organizer Russ Malkin will take guests behind the scenes of adventures filmed across more than 160 countries.

Recent findings suggest that also joining the Aurora will be engineer, doctor and astronaut Robert Thirsk; Indianapolis 500 racing driver Lyn St. James; Olympic gold medalist Dr Rochelle Stevens; and film critic, author and broadcaster James King.

Industry observers note that the Iona’s 35-night cruise will welcome Olympic, World and Commonwealth champion Christine Ohuruogu. She will be joined by long-serving royal correspondent Simon Vigar and former SAS soldier Colin Maclachlan, who will share insights from his career and experiences in the special forces.

The special guest program will run from January to April 2027, with individual speakers joining selected sections of Arcadia’s world cruise, Aurora’s grand tour and Iona’s 35-night cruise.

P&O Cruises’ Black Friday sale offers savings of up to £500 per cabin* on hundreds of holidays, plus a Black Friday Price Drop Guarantee, available until midnight on December 1, 2026.

Obviously nothing beats a frothy PSL on a crisp autumn day (bonus points if you are unabashedly wearing UGGs), but we're here to talk about an even more iconic cozy szn tradition: the annual Starbucks red cup (or the Starbucks holiday cup). As anyone who grew up in the early 2000s knows, Starbucks red cups were an absolute hallmark of the holidays. Truly, there was nothing like begging your mom to drop you off at the mall so you could lurk around, brand-fresh red cup in hand, and hit up, IDK, American Eagle Outfitters.

Red cups have been going strong since the late ’90s—they launched in 1997, to be exact, when they weren't even red, but more on that later. And every year, the cup has a brand-new design…sometimes multiple! So, now that the new 2026 red cups have been unveiled (scroll all the way down to see them!), the time has come to find out which Starbucks red cup sparked joy the year you were born.

Industry observers note that before we begin, apologies to all the millennials out there, but red cups simply weren't a thing from 1981 to 1996. However, please feel free to personally identify with the holiday cup of your choice (or the cup from the year you started drinking coffee)—OR just take a cozy walk down memory lane. #31271. Tech Report: The One Record in Sports That Will Never Be Broken

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (404 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The One Record in Sports That Will Never Be Broken

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (404 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that back in my full-time sportswriting days—and, in fact, throughout my journalism career—I managed to disguise my fundamental innumeracy.
  • In this era of analytics and the tyranny of numbers, there is one statistic that remains not only my favorite but that is likely never to fall, and it comes from, of all sports, hockey.
  • Sources indicate that the first time I ever saw Gretzky play was during the 1988 Stanley Cup playoffs, when my Boston Bruins faced his Edmonton Oilers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No one told me there would be math.

Recent findings suggest that back in my full-time sportswriting days—and, in fact, throughout my journalism career—I managed to disguise my fundamental innumeracy. Then suddenly, quite recently, numbers became paramount in sports. Baseball led the way, as it does in so many areas where boredom is involved. Now, thanks to gambling’s explosion in popularity, statistics have become one of the primary ways to be a fan.

In this era of analytics and the tyranny of numbers, there is one statistic that remains not only my favorite but that is likely never to fall, and it comes from, of all sports, hockey. It is this, which boggles the mind: Wayne Gretzky ended his career in 1999 with a total of 2,857 points, which includes goals and assists. Factor out the goals, and he’s still at 1,963, which is 42 more points than the player with the next-highest total, Jaromir Jagr, who is retired.

Sources indicate that the first time I ever saw Gretzky play was during the 1988 Stanley Cup playoffs, when my Boston Bruins faced his Edmonton Oilers. These were the dynastic Oilers, loaded with talent: Mark Messier. Jari Kurri. Glenn Anderson. Grant Fuhr between the pipes. All of them Hall of Famers. Amid all this clamorous talent, Gretzky was a phantom. He had this strange and wonderful ability to vanish in the middle of the action and then, suddenly, appear in exactly the right spot at exactly the right time to make exactly the right play.

In a recent development, gretzky will likely be the leading point scorer in NHL history for the next several decades. In fact, you have to go all the way down to seventh place on the list to find an active player, Sidney Crosby, who is 202 short of Gretzky’s 1,963 assist-only number. Another active player, Alex Ovechkin, is in tenth place, but he’s got one skate out the door already. The next active players on the list are Evgeni Malkin and Patrick Kane, at 23rd and 24th.

Like Gretzky himself, this statistic disappears among all the more notable numbers until it suddenly pops out to amaze and astound. I like Sidney Crosby a great deal as a player, but I hope he never gets there.

Charles P Pierce is the author of four books, most recently Idiot America, and has been a working journalist since 1976.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Fall has the singular ability to turn even the most Spartan man into a bit of a style savant. It’s like a wolf awakens the second that temperatures start to drop. Suddenly you see an Instagram post from the junior analyst below you; he must fancy himself a budding A$AP Rocky, because he’s rocking a statement scarf. Your brother-in-law is wearing a turtleneck. Your buddy is in white jeans. Every day, you zone out in dumb stakeholder meetings and fantasize about a new jacket or that pair of buttery-soft leather loafers you saw on a dude at the grocery store.

Recent findings suggest that it’s because fall invites more—more layers, more textures. It can be freeing. No more worrying if that T-shirt will become a body scan of where and how you sweat; no more worrying if those pants will suffocate you. But ... it can be too much. How should you layer? How can you get funky for the holiday party without looking like an asshole? What brands are even worth buying?

We answer all those questions elsewhere in this magazine, but today we want you to take a breath. Keep it simple. How? By following some good examples.

Industry observers note that A lot of the best-dressed guys right now are trimming down their wardrobes in favor of focusing on the basics. “This fall I’ve tried to trim the fat and make do with a much smaller wardrobe,” claims actor, content creator, and friend of the magazine Albert Muzquiz—better known online by his handle @edgyalbert. “I only have a few shirts, a few pants, and a couple jackets—and I feel like I’m dressing better than ever.”.

Sources indicate that so instead of lobbing a bunch of meaningless trends, or -cores, at you, we decided to send you to some of the best-dressed men of the moment. You’ve heard enough from us; here’s what they’re feeling this fall.

Recent findings suggest that jake Mueser, founder of the eponymous bespoke suiting brand J. Mueser, has a handful of fall essentials. That cohort includes a cream turtleneck, which “you can throw on with anything,” as well as a classic tweed or herringbone blazer—same idea. They’re easy but plenty damn sexy.

Sources indicate that mueser also extols the virtues of a classic flannel suit—perhaps like the one he makes. “It works with everything from a denim shirt to a tie,” he notes. “I like to break it up, wearing the jacket with vintage light-wash Wrangler cowboy cuts.” (A move we wholeheartedly endorse.).

Industry observers note that J. Mueser Waverly Herringbone Virgin Wool-Tweed Blazer.

It has been revealed that J. Mueser Ivory Chunky Merino Roll-Neck Sweater.

Sources indicate that J. Mueser Charcoal Churchill Stripe Flannel Waverly Suit.

Recent findings suggest that there are a few reasons Drew Thomas can’t stop recommending merino sweaters—the thin, almost jersey sort—to his more than 500,000 TikTok followers. “You can get so much wear out of one,” he claims. “You can layer it in the fall, wear it on its own on a slightly warmer day, or tie it around your shoulders. It works in the spring too, and even on a summer night when it gets a little cooler.”.

Another seasonally versatile piece Thomas will stand ten toes down for is cream pants. In fact, Thomas likes to wear his all through fall. He keeps a few pairs on constant rotation. “I feel like the cream breaks up those darker fall colors and lets them stand out more,” he states.

According to recent reports, when it comes to his next fall investment, Thomas is taking cues from the British sartorial invasion (“It never really went away, but it definitely feels like it’s having a moment again”) and looking to Barbour. “Something timeless and practical that I can wear for years and that only gets better with age,” he notes. “I love the idea of owning something that develops character over time and could eventually be passed down to someone else. Those are the kinds of pieces I feel are worth investing in.”.

Buck Mason Hollywood Pleated Trouser.

J. Crew Relaxed-Fit Double-Pleated Corduroy Pant.

It has been revealed that “A down vest is my favorite fall garment,” Esquire contributor Christopher Fenimore told us. “It’s an easy outerwear piece to layer stuff under. I run hot, and I like having parts of my body exposed to the elements.”.

In a recent development, we second that, but more predictably he highlights the entire category of shirting. Jackets and layers get a lot of shine, but this is the layer that, no matter how much temperatures fluctuate, will be on the skin. It’s a great time to get a few good oxford-cloth button-downs, polos, or beefier tees.

This time of year is also a great time to get clinical. “I assess things I have that might need updates, in terms of fit and silhouette or different fabrications depending on how I’d wear them,” he indicates. That can be rebuying your preferred undershirt or socks, or it could be a good time to jump on that thinner, more versatile merino sweater wave.

Rocky Mountain Featherbed Down Vest.

“Fall is the best time to break in a newly introduced pair of denim,” Muzquiz indicates. Wear it hard enough now and “it’ll be soft enough and possibly breathable enough for wear during the spring and parts of the summer.” No better time to get something esoteric.

Industry observers note that when it comes to fall shoes, Muzquiz is into a classic six-inch lace-up boot. “There are so many bullshit brands out there that are trying to fool you with budget options,” he claims. “Just get a pair of Red Wing Heritage if you’re starting out or Viberg if you really wanna flex.”.

Recent findings suggest that muzquiz also finds himself taking part in the “buttery, delicate loafer movement” that’s been picking up steam as of late. The Yardee Moccasin loafers from Vinny’s are his pick of the bunch.

Viberg Navvy Boot - Brandy Hatch Grain Calf.

Every Other Thursday Cashmere V-neck Knit.

Vinny’s Yardee Nappa Leather Loafer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Carrie Coon had a question for her fellow Women in Hollywood honorees: “Can we start a studio?”.

On Monday night, the actress took the stage at ELLE’s 2026 Women in Hollywood celebration in Los Angeles, where she called for women in the entertainment industry to come together and create more opportunities for themselves.

Coon was introduced by her Gilded Age co-star Louisa Jacobson, who celebrated her recent career achievements.

It has been revealed that “Carrie is a crusader, always fighting tirelessly for artistic integrity in a landscape that seems to value high gloss and profit over honest, nuanced storytelling,” Jacobson remarked. “And if you know Carrie, you know that she is completely allergic to superficiality.”.

In her acceptance speech, Coon reflected on the importance of women’s stories, drawing inspiration from feminist literature and End Times Fascism, a book by Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor.

“Patriarchy, capitalism...these are hierarchical systems of domination that rely on fear,” she said. “And in this paradigm, women and girls, like our natural resources, are a disposable commodity—and as such, according to philosopher Kate Manne—our stories are interchangeable and of equal power. But of course, they’re not. That’s not true. And we’re not a monolith.”.

Coon went on to discuss the performances of her fellow honorees, arguing that their work represented something extraordinary. “In these women, I see the fight for the living world. I see moral clarity. I see imagination. I see courage,” she mentioned. “And these are, in fact, the antidotes to fascism. That’s how notable this storytelling is.”.

Toward the end of her speech, Coon questioned how women in Hollywood could create lasting change beyond events celebrating their individual achievements.

“How do we forge our collective safety and solidarity in an ethic of communalism?” she asked. “Okay, so this is the part of the speech where I don’t actually have the answer to that question, but I make the appeal that nights like these shouldn’t be one-off nights.”.

She concluded with the aforementioned proposition for her peers: “And so I’m going to start with a really stupid question, but I’m not afraid to ask a stupid question: Can we start a studio?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Princess of Wales, best known as Kate Middleton, had a slightly awkward moment on her tour of India this week (where she’s raising awareness for her husband Prince William’s Earthshot Prize Awards, which reward innovative environmental solutions). While greeting an excited crowd gathered in Mumbai, the Princess sadly had to disappoint a cluster of children who were hoping to get her autograph.

Speaking to one child who had a pen and paper in hand for the Princess, Catherine reportedly had to say, “Sorry, I can’t!” as to sign her name would be a severe breach of royal protocol.

None of the royal family are allowed to give out autographs, owing to fears that their signature could be replicated and forged, or that they’ll simply be sold on for monetary gain.

In recent years, they have become more amenable to people requesting selfies, which previously was not common practice.

It’s far from the first time the Princess has had to navigate this type of delicate situation with a member of the public; earlier this year while on a visit to Wales, she was also asked to sign her name and had to offer up a consolatory handshake instead.

The trip to India is Kate’s first international visit since her cancer diagnosis in 2024, and her attendance was somewhat unexpected. She has missed the last three Earthshot Prize ceremonies, but given she’s traveled all the way to Mumbai, it’s not a surprise that she revealed up alongside William for this year’s event, wearing a stunning Anarkali by Indian designer Mahima Mahajan.

The 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony will not air live but will be available to watch on Amazon Prime from November 30.

According to recent reports, elizabeth Debicki knows that no career is built alone. On Monday night, the actress accepted her honor at ELLE’s 2026 Women in Hollywood celebration, taking a moment to recognize the people who helped make her career possible.

After being introduced by Alexander Skarsgård, Debicki thanked her fellow honorees before reflecting on the support she has received throughout her journey.

“I really love to work. It is my great love,” she said. “And standing here tonight, I feel a really deep sense of gratitude for all the people—the small army of people—who have fought for me to be able to do my work.”.

Recent findings suggest that debicki recalled how casting director Ronna Kress helped her secure an audition for Baz Luhrmann’s The Great Gatsby, which became her breakout film role. At the time, she was just 20 years old, had recently graduated from drama school in Australia, and had never done a screen test.

In a recent development, “Now, Baz, who is my fairy godfather, he fought very, very hard for me after I auditioned for him,” she explained. “But the only reason I was able to get that audition was because Ronna Kress watched the shoddy rookie tape I made back home and somehow managed to convince Baz to sit still long enough to watch it (which, if you know, you know is an actual miracle).”.

Industry observers note that she continued, “Ronna fought very, very hard for the studio to fly me out here to L.A.—I had never been here before—and to read for the part. And truly, that changed everything. That was really, really my door. And Ronna and Baz, they held that open for me.”.

Debicki also praised the other women being recognized that evening: Julianne Moore, Penélope Cruz, Florence Pugh, Inde Navarette, Rosalind Eleazar, and Carrie Coon.

In a recent development, “In your work, your audiences are so privileged to witness your talent and your intelligence,” she said. “And this generosity in the way that you work, it makes us feel sane, and it makes us feel seen. So thank you, so, so much.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, coming back home isn’t easy, especially for Luke Grimes. The Yellowstone actor spent all of the hit Taylor Sheridan drama as Kayce Dutton, a man trying to leave the past behind and move on from the sins of his father, family patriarch John Dutton (Kevin Costner). But when the western ended and Grimes had to say goodbye to the cast, crew, and his onscreen wife Kelsey Asbille (who played Monica Dutton), he really thought it was for the last time.

“Hopefully everyone can see that it was time,” Grimes told Esquire when Yellowstone ended. “There’s always talks of spin-offs. I’d do it [but] I just don’t understand how it would work once the story ends. Kayce wants to cowboy and be happy with his family. He doesn’t want to kill people anymore. He doesn’t want the weight of a huge mega ranch that isn’t sustainable in today’s times. He wants his little slice of heaven. It’s that simple.”.

Paramount offered Grimes the option to return anyway on Marshals, a spin-off of Yellowstone that sees Kayce Dutton join the U.S. Marshals service in Montana. Reportedly, they won him over after pitching that they would take everything from Kayce so that he would be forced to start again. First on the chopping block? His wife, Monica.

“The thing I was most worried about doing Marshals was doing it without Kelsey,” Grimes told ScreenRant during an interview for season 2 last week. “I just couldn’t wrap my head around Kayce without Monica. That was the story. The rest of Yellowstone was about people fighting over land, and I just loved my wife. I had my own thing going on, and so I didn’t know what that would even look like.”.

Recent findings suggest that eventually he came around to the idea. “Once I sort of, you know, could wrap my head around the fact that that was going to open up all these fresh storylines,” he admitted, “we just [had] to make sure we do honor [their life together] and don’t try to skip over it or pretend it didn’t happen.”.

Marshals season 2 continues to air this fall, as Kayce Dutton explores a potential latest relationship with fellow Marshal Andrea Cruz (Ash Santos). Sometime this season, former Yellowstone fan favorite Jimmy (Jefferson White) will also make an appearance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

King Charles and Queen Camilla had the best response to the long-awaited news that Twilight and Batman legend Robert Pattinson is set to become the new James Bond.

The royal family has long been associated with the iconic British spy series, with the King and Queen—along with Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales—attending the No Time to Die premiere at London’s Royal Albert Hall in September 2021 (the last film that was released in the long-running franchise).

In response to the official James Bond X account sharing the news about Pattinson, the royal family's account (which acts as a news source for the King and Queen), re-shared the post along with the comment: “Welcome to His Majesty’s Secret Service, Mr Bond.”.

So far, the quip has been liked over 250,000 times.

Prior to the 2021 premiere, the King had attended plenty of other screenings of the Bond series—dating as far back as 1981 for the launch of For Your Eyes Only, which had Roger Moore starring as the fictional MI6 agent.

The late Princess Diana and Princess Margaret also turned out for that particular premiere.

Commenting on his major career leap, Robert Pattinson noted in a statement, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime.”.

Industry observers note that he continued, “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

Filming is expected to begin early next year, with an unspecified release date slated for sometime in 2028.

It will be the first James Bond movie produced by Amazon MGM, after the Broccoli family unexpectedly sold the rights in 2025.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on Monday, November 16, Princess Kate and Prince William landed in Mumbai, India, for their first overseas royal tour in four years. The last time the pair made an international state visit was when they traveled to the Caribbean in the spring of 2022 to celebrate the late Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee.

In a recent development, now, the Prince and Princess of Wales have hit the road again for the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards, which are being hosted in Asia for the first time ever. The annual prize, founded by Prince William with an inaugural ceremony in 2021 and set to last until 2030, celebrates innovators who are breaking ground in the environmentalism space.

While it was announced back in February that William would be traveling for the ceremony, it was confirmed only this past weekend that Kate would be joining him. This marks her first major trip with William since her 2024 cancer diagnosis and eventual remission (she also took a solo trip to Italy this May).

Industry observers note that the 2026 Earthshot ceremony takes place on November 17, but Kate and William are spending a total of three days in India. They began their trip with a visit to Ballard Estate, the business and shopping district of Mumbai. There, the Prince and Princess of Wales played a bit of gully cricket, took a ride on the metro, and visited local vendors and performers. Then, on day two, they stopped by the Bandra Worli Sea Link promenade and attended the Children’s Earthshot ceremony before dressing up for the official event.

For the rest of their time abroad, the royals will be “celebrating innovation, sustainability, youth leadership, and the enduring connections between the United Kingdom and India,” per their office at Kensington Palace.

Ahead, see all the best photos of Kate and William from their overseas tour of Mumbai.

The Prince and Princess of Wales paid homage to Indian culture as they attended the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Awards tonight in Mumbai.

Recent findings suggest that after a busy day of engagements (and outfit changes), the couple made it to the Jio World Convention Centre to celebrate global change-makers who are actively working to solve urgent environmental problems. It was the first time the awards were held in India, and the event brought together around 5,000 global guests, world leaders, and celebrities.

And for the momentous evening, the British royals wore traditional Indian attire.

The stunning long-sleeve piece had gold and green embroidery throughout, and Kate expertly accessorized it with jewelry from Queen Elizabeth II’s fabulous emerald tassel suite. Up top, she wore the late monarch’s luxurious diamond-and-emerald tassel drop earrings, while around her neck, the matching tassel necklace took the spotlight.

The suite is believed to have been gifted to Queen Elizabeth by Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan of Abu Dhabi during the 1989 United Arab Emirates state visit to Britain. And through the years, the monarch took it out for several vital occasions, including for the Return Dinner hosted in 2011 by President Barack Obama and first lady Michelle Obama at the end of their state visit to the United Kingdom.

In 2022, the queen loaned the suite to Kate, who wore the necklace and earrings to the state dinner hosted by the Governor General of Jamaica. Now, it’s become a shining standout in her royal jewelry collection.
